title.zh: 卷49 列傳第41 異域上（高句麗・百濟・蠻・獠・宕昌・鄧至・白蘭・氐・稽胡・庫莫奚）
title.en: Volume 49 Biographies 41: Other Regions 1 (Goguryeo; Baekje; Man; Tanchang; Bailan; Di; Jihu; Kumo Xi)
title.raw: 卷49 列傳第41 異域上（高句麗・百濟・蠻・獠・宕昌・鄧至・白蘭・氐・稽胡・庫莫奚） Volume 49 Biographies 41: Other Regions 1 (Goguryeo; Baekje; Man; Tanchang; Bailan; Di; Jihu; Kumo Xi)

sentences.zh: 異域上

translations.literal: Other Regions, Part One
translations.idiomatic: Other Regions, Part One

sentences.zh: 蓋天地之所覆載，至大矣；

translations.literal: For that which heaven and earth cover and bear up is supremely great;
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth cover and sustain all things—nothing is greater;

sentences.zh: 日月之所臨照，至廣矣。

translations.literal: that which sun and moon look down upon and shine upon is supremely broad.
translations.idiomatic: and what the sun and moon illuminate stretches without limit.

sentences.zh: 然則萬物之內，民人寡而禽獸多；

translations.literal: Thus within the myriad things, human people are few while birds and beasts are many;
translations.idiomatic: Yet among living creatures, people are few and beasts are many;

sentences.zh: 兩儀之間，中土局而庶俗曠。

translations.literal: between the Two Principles, the Central Land is cramped while the many customs of the periphery are vast.
translations.idiomatic: between heaven and earth the central realm is narrow while the borderlands are vast.

sentences.zh: 求之鄒說，詭怪之迹實繁；

translations.literal: If one seeks it in Zou Yan's theories, traces of the bizarre and uncanny are truly numerous;
translations.idiomatic: Zou Yan's cosmology teems with strange and uncanny tales;

sentences.zh: 考之《山經》，奇譎之詞匪一。

translations.literal: if one examines the Classic of Mountains and Seas, outlandish and fantastic expressions are not one alone.
translations.idiomatic: the Classic of Mountains and Seas abounds in fantastic language.

sentences.zh: 周、孔存而不論，是非紛而莫辯。

translations.literal: Zhou and Confucius preserved these matters without discussing them; right and wrong were tangled and could not be distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius and the Zhou sages left such matters unspoken, and truth and falsehood became impossible to sort out.

sentences.zh: 秦皇鞭笞天下，黷武於遐方；

translations.literal: The First Emperor of Qin flogged the realm and indulged in martial excess in distant regions;
translations.idiomatic: Qin Shihuang scourged the empire and squandered arms on distant campaigns;

sentences.zh: 漢武士馬強盛，肆志於遠畧。

translations.literal: the martial power of Han had strong soldiers and horses and indulged its will in far-reaching designs.
translations.idiomatic: Han Wudi, with armies and horses at peak strength, pursued grand designs far from home.

sentences.zh: 匈奴旣卻，其國已虛；

translations.literal: Once the Xiongnu had been driven off, their state was already hollow;
translations.idiomatic: When the Xiongnu were beaten back, their lands lay empty;

sentences.zh: 犬馬旣來，其民亦困。

translations.literal: once dogs and horses had come in tribute, their people were also exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: when tribute horses arrived at court, the common people were exhausted as well.

sentences.zh: 是知鴈海龍堆，天所以絕夷夏也；

translations.literal: From this one knows that the wild-goose sea and Dragon Mound are what Heaven uses to cut off Yi and Xia;
translations.idiomatic: Thus the wild seas and Dragon Mound are Heaven's barrier between barbarian and Chinese realms;

sentences.zh: 炎方朔漠，地所以限內外也。

translations.literal: the fiery south and northern deserts are what Earth uses to demarcate inner and outer.
translations.idiomatic: the torrid south and northern wastes are Earth's line between inner and outer lands.

sentences.zh: 況乎時非秦、漢，志甚嬴、劉，違天道以求其功，殫民力而從所欲，顛墜之釁，固不旋踵。

translations.literal: How much more when the age was not Qin or Han, yet the will rivaled that of Ying and Liu—defying Heaven's Way to seek achievement, exhausting the people's strength to follow one's desires: the omen of collapse would surely come without turning the heel.
translations.idiomatic: How much worse when rulers were no Qin or Han emperors yet aspired like Ying Zheng and the Liu emperors—defying Heaven's way for glory, draining the people for private ends: ruin would follow in no time at all.

sentences.zh: 是以先王設教，內諸夏而外夷狄；

translations.literal: Therefore the former kings established instruction, keeping the many Xia within and placing the Yi and Di without;
translations.idiomatic: The ancient kings taught accordingly: civilization within, barbarians without;

sentences.zh: 往哲垂範，美樹德而鄙廣地。

translations.literal: the sages of old handed down models, prizing the cultivation of virtue and disdaining broad territory.
translations.idiomatic: sages of old prized virtue and scorned mere territorial gain.

sentences.zh: 雖禹迹之東漸西被，不過海及流沙；

translations.literal: Although Yu's traces extended east and spread west, they did not go beyond the sea and flowing sands;
translations.idiomatic: Even Yu's dominion, spreading east and west, reached only to the sea and the shifting sands;

sentences.zh: 王制之自北徂南，裁稱穴居交趾。

translations.literal: the royal regulations from north to south barely named cave-dwellers and Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: the royal domain from north to south barely acknowledged cave-dwellers and Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 豈非道貫三古，義高百代者乎。

translations.literal: Is this not a Way that runs through the three antiquities and a principle loftier than a hundred generations?
translations.idiomatic: Is this not a Way spanning three ages and a principle towering above a hundred generations?

sentences.zh: 有周承喪亂之後，屬戰爭之日，定四表以武功，安三邊以權道。

translations.literal: Zhou inherited after the age of mourning and chaos, in days belonging to warfare; it settled the four quarters by martial achievement and secured the three frontiers by expedient policy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou rose after an age of mourning and chaos, in a time of constant war; it pacified the four quarters by arms and steadied the three frontiers through flexible statecraft.

sentences.zh: 趙、魏尚梗，則結姻於北狄；

translations.literal: When Zhao and Wei still resisted, it formed marriage ties with the northern Di;
translations.idiomatic: While Zhao and Wei still held out, Zhou sealed marriage alliances with northern tribes;

sentences.zh: 廄庫未實，則通好於西戎。

translations.literal: when the stables and granaries were not yet full, it opened friendly relations with the western Rong.
translations.idiomatic: when granaries and stables were still empty, it courted friendship with western tribes.

sentences.zh: 由是德刑具舉，聲名遐洎。

translations.literal: Thereby virtue and punishment were both deployed, and fame and sound reached distant shores.
translations.idiomatic: Thus virtue and punishment worked together, and Zhou's renown spread to distant lands.

sentences.zh: 卉服氈裘，輻協於屬國；

translations.literal: Men in flowery dress and fur coats converged in submission at the dependent states;
translations.idiomatic: Tribes in painted robes and fur coats gathered at the border dependencies;

sentences.zh: 商胡販客，填委於旗亭。

translations.literal: Sogdian merchants and traders piled up goods at the relay pavilions.
translations.idiomatic: Sogdian traders packed the market stalls along the highways.

sentences.zh: 雖東畧漏三吳之地，南巡阻百越之境，而國威之所肅服，風化之所覃被，亦足為弘矣。

translations.literal: Although eastern campaigns missed the lands of the Three Wu and southern tours were blocked by the lands of the Hundred Yue, yet what the state's majesty awed into submission and what civilizing influence spread over was still ample enough to be called grand.
translations.idiomatic: Though eastern campaigns never fully held the Three Wu and southern tours could not penetrate the Hundred Yue, the awe of Zhou power and the reach of its civilizing influence were grand enough by any measure.

sentences.zh: 其四夷來朝聘者，今竝紀之於後。

translations.literal: Those of the four Yi who came to court and present tribute are now all recorded together below.
translations.idiomatic: The foreign peoples who came to court with tribute are recorded in what follows.

sentences.zh: 至於道路遠近，物產風俗，詳諸前史，或有不同。

translations.literal: As for the distance of roads, local products, and customs, the former histories treat them in detail, and there are sometimes differences.
translations.idiomatic: Distances, products, and customs are set out at length in earlier histories, though accounts sometimes differ.

sentences.zh: 斯皆錄其當時所記，以備遺闕云爾。

translations.literal: These are all recorded as noted in their own day, to supply what might otherwise be missing.
translations.idiomatic: What follows records contemporary accounts to fill gaps in the record.

sentences.zh: 高句麗

translations.literal: Goguryeo
translations.idiomatic: Goguryeo

sentences.zh: 高麗者，其先出於夫餘。

translations.literal: Goryeo—that is, Goguryeo—had its forebears from Buyeo.
translations.idiomatic: Goguryeo traced its origins to Buyeo.

sentences.zh: 自言始祖曰朱蒙，河伯女感日影所孕也。

translations.literal: They themselves say their founding ancestor was Jumong, born when the River Lord's daughter conceived after being moved by the sun's reflection.
translations.idiomatic: They claimed their founder Jumong was born when a daughter of the River Lord conceived after the sun's reflection touched her.

sentences.zh: 朱蒙長而有材畧，夫餘人惡而逐之。

translations.literal: When Jumong grew up he had talent and stratagem; the people of Buyeo hated him and drove him out.
translations.idiomatic: Jumong grew gifted and resourceful; the Buyeo people hated him and drove him away.

sentences.zh: 土于紇斗骨城，自號曰高句麗，仍以高為氏。

translations.literal: He settled at Kogolbone Fortress, styled himself Goguryeo, and took Gao as his clan name.
translations.idiomatic: He settled at Kogolbone Fortress, called his state Goguryeo, and took Gao as his clan name.

sentences.zh: 其孫莫來漸盛，擊夫餘而臣之。

translations.literal: His grandson Molae gradually grew powerful, struck Buyeo, and made it his subject.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Molae grew strong, attacked Buyeo, and brought it under submission.

sentences.zh: 莫來裔孫璉，始通使於後魏。

translations.literal: Lian, a descendant of Molae's line, first sent envoys to the Later Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Lian, a descendant in Molae's line, first sent envoys to Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 其地，東至新羅，西渡遼水二千里，南接百濟，北鄰靺鞨千餘里。

translations.literal: Its territory extended east to Silla, west across the Liao River for two thousand li, south adjoining Baekje, and north bordering the Mohe for more than a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Its lands ran east to Silla, two thousand li west across the Liao River, south to Baekje, and north to the Mohe for more than a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 治平壤城。

translations.literal: The capital was governed from Pyongyang.
translations.idiomatic: The court sat at Pyongyang.

sentences.zh: 其城，東西六里，南臨浿水。

translations.literal: The city was six li from east to west and faced the Yalu River on the south.
translations.idiomatic: The city measured six li east to west and stood on the Yalu River to the south.

sentences.zh: 城內唯積倉儲器備，寇賊至日，方入固守。

translations.literal: Within the city they only stored grain and equipment; when bandits came, only then did people enter to hold fast.
translations.idiomatic: Inside they kept only grain stores and equipment; when raiders came, the people entered to hold the walls.

sentences.zh: 王則別為宅於其側，不常居之。

translations.literal: The king maintained a separate residence beside it and did not dwell there regularly.
translations.idiomatic: The king kept a separate residence nearby and did not live in the city itself.

sentences.zh: 其外有國內城及漢城，亦別都也，復有遼東、玄菟等數十城，皆置官司，以相統攝。

translations.literal: Outside were the Inner City and Han City, also secondary capitals; there were also several dozen cities such as Liaodong and Xuantu, each with officials appointed to oversee them.
translations.idiomatic: Outside lay the Inner City and Han City, secondary capitals as well; dozens of cities such as Liaodong and Xuantu each had officials to govern them.

sentences.zh: 大官有大對盧，次有太大兄、大兄、小兄、意俟奢、烏拙、太大使者、大使者、小使者、褥奢、翳屬、仙人幷褥薩凡十三等，分掌內外事焉。

translations.literal: Among great offices there was the Great Tolu, next the Great Elder Brother, Elder Brother, Lesser Elder Brother, Uisoksa, Uchok, Great Envoy, Envoy, Lesser Envoy, Yuksa, Uisok, Immortal together with Yuksa—thirteen ranks in all—dividing administration of inner and outer affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Senior offices included the Great Tolu, then the Great Elder Brother, Elder Brother, Lesser Elder Brother, Uisoksa, Uchok, Great Envoy, Envoy, Lesser Envoy, Yuksa, Uisok, Immortal, and Yuksa—thirteen ranks in all—governing internal and external affairs.

sentences.zh: 其大對盧，則以彊弱相陵，奪而自為之，不由王之署置也。

translations.literal: As for the Great Tolu, the strong overbear the weak and seize the post for themselves; it is not conferred by the king's appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Tolu was seized by whichever faction was strongest, not appointed by the king.

sentences.zh: 其刑法：謀反及叛者，先以火焚爇，然後斬首，籍沒其家。

translations.literal: Their penal code: for plotting rebellion or defection, the culprit was first burned with fire, then beheaded, and the household registered and confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Penal law held that rebels and defectors were burned alive, then beheaded, and their households confiscated.

sentences.zh: 盜者，十餘倍徵贓。

translations.literal: Thieves paid restitution at more than ten times the value.
translations.idiomatic: Thieves paid restitution at more than tenfold the stolen goods.

sentences.zh: 若貧不能備，及負公私債者，皆聽評其子女為奴婢以償之。

translations.literal: If the poor could not make payment, or if one owed public or private debts, both were allowed to appraise sons and daughters as male and female slaves to repay.
translations.idiomatic: Those too poor to pay, or in debt to public or private creditors, might assign sons and daughters as slaves to settle the account.

sentences.zh: 丈夫衣同袖衫、大口褲、白韋帶、黃革履。

translations.literal: Men wore tunics with shared sleeves, baggy trousers, white leather belts, and yellow leather shoes.
translations.idiomatic: Men wore tunics with shared sleeves, wide trousers, white leather belts, and yellow leather shoes.

sentences.zh: 其冠曰骨蘇，多以紫羅為之，雜以金銀為飾。

translations.literal: Their cap was called gusu, mostly made of purple gauze, mixed with gold and silver for ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Their cap, called gusu, was chiefly purple gauze adorned with gold and silver.

sentences.zh: 其有官品者，又插二鳥羽於其上，以顯異之。

translations.literal: Those who held official rank also inserted two bird feathers on top to show distinction.
translations.idiomatic: Officials added two bird feathers to the cap to mark their rank.

sentences.zh: 婦人服裙襦，裾袖皆為袂。

translations.literal: Women wore skirts and jackets; hems and sleeves were all made as overlapping panels.
translations.idiomatic: Women wore skirts and jackets with overlapping hems and sleeves.

sentences.zh: 書籍有《五經》、《三史》、《三國志》、《晉陽秋》。

translations.literal: Books included the Five Classics, the Three Histories, Records of the Three Kingdoms, and the Jin Annals.
translations.idiomatic: They possessed the Five Classics, the Three Histories, Records of the Three Kingdoms, and the Jin Annals.

sentences.zh: 兵器有甲弩弓箭戟矟矛鋋。

translations.literal: Weapons included armor, crossbows, bows, arrows, halberds, spears, and daggers.
translations.idiomatic: Their arms included armor, crossbows, bows, arrows, halberds, spears, and daggers.

sentences.zh: 賦稅則絹布及粟，隨其所有，量貧富差等輸之。

translations.literal: Taxes were silk cloth and grain, according to what each possessed, assessed by wealth in graded payments.
translations.idiomatic: Taxes were paid in silk, cloth, and grain according to means, in graded amounts by wealth.

sentences.zh: 土田塉薄，居處節儉。

translations.literal: The soil was thin and poor; in dwelling they were frugal.
translations.idiomatic: The land was poor and thin; people lived frugally.

sentences.zh: 然尚容止。

translations.literal: Yet they still valued deportment.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they still valued proper bearing.

sentences.zh: 多詐偽，言辭鄙穢，不簡親疏，乃至同川而浴，共室而寢。

translations.literal: They were much given to deceit; speech was coarse and foul; they did not distinguish near from far, even bathing in the same stream and sleeping in the same room.
translations.idiomatic: They were deceitful, their speech coarse; kin and stranger alike bathed in the same stream and slept in one room.

sentences.zh: 風俗好淫，不以為愧。

translations.literal: Custom favored licentiousness and did not treat it as shame.
translations.idiomatic: Licentiousness was common custom and no cause for shame.

sentences.zh: 有游女者，夫無常人。

translations.literal: There were wandering women who had no fixed husbands.
translations.idiomatic: Some women wandered without fixed husbands.

sentences.zh: 婚娶之禮，畧無財幣，若受財者，謂之賣婢，俗甚恥之。

translations.literal: Marriage rites had almost no bride-price; if one accepted wealth, it was called selling a maidservant, and the custom greatly shamed this.
translations.idiomatic: Marriage involved almost no bride-price; accepting payment was deemed selling a daughter and deeply shameful.

sentences.zh: 父母及夫喪，其服制同於華夏。

translations.literal: Mourning for parents and husbands followed the same regulations as the Central States.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning for parents and husbands followed Chinese practice.

sentences.zh: 兄弟則限以三月。

translations.literal: For brothers mourning was limited to three months.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning for brothers lasted three months.

sentences.zh: 敬信佛法，尤好淫祀。

translations.literal: They revered the Buddhist Law and especially favored licentious sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: They revered Buddhism and especially favored extravagant cult sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 又有神廟二所：一曰夫餘神，刻木作婦人之象；

translations.literal: There were also two spirit shrines: one called the Buyeo Spirit, carved in wood as a woman's image;
translations.idiomatic: They maintained two spirit shrines: the Buyeo Spirit, a wooden image of a woman;

sentences.zh: 一曰登高神，云是其始祖夫餘神之子。

translations.literal: one called the Ascent Spirit, said to be the son of the founding Buyeo Spirit.
translations.idiomatic: and the Ascent Spirit, said to be son of the Buyeo founding spirit.

sentences.zh: 竝置官司，遣人守護。

translations.literal: Both had officials appointed and men sent to guard them.
translations.idiomatic: Both had officials appointed to guard them.

sentences.zh: 蓋河伯女與朱蒙云。

translations.literal: This refers to the tale of the River Lord's daughter and Jumong.
translations.idiomatic: This commemorates the legend of the River Lord's daughter and Jumong.

sentences.zh: 璉五世孫成，大統十二年，遣使獻其方物。

translations.literal: Cheng, fifth-generation descendant of Lian, in the twelfth year of Datong sent envoys presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng, Lian's descendant five generations removed, sent tribute in the twelfth year of Datong.

sentences.zh: 成死，子湯立。

translations.literal: When Cheng died, his son Tang succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng died, his son Tang succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 建德六年，湯又遣使來貢。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jiande, Tang again sent envoys to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Jiande, Tang again sent tribute envoys.

sentences.zh: 高祖拜湯為上開府儀同大將軍、遼東郡開國公、遼東王。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu appointed Tang Superior Opening Office, Peer of Threefold Honours with Grand General, Duke Who Founded Liaodong Commandery, and King of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu appointed Tang Superior Opening Office, Peer of Threefold Honours with Grand General, founding duke of Liaodong Commandery, and King of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 百濟者，其先蓋馬韓之屬國，夫餘之別種。

translations.literal: Baekje: its forebears were probably a dependent state of the Ma Han and a separate branch of Buyeo.
translations.idiomatic: Baekje probably descended from a Ma Han dependency and a Buyeo offshoot.

sentences.zh: 有仇台者，始國於帶方。

translations.literal: There was Qiutai, who first founded a state at Daifang.
translations.idiomatic: Qiutai first founded a state at Daifang.

sentences.zh: 故其地界東極新羅，北接高句麗，西南俱限大海。

translations.literal: Thus its borders reached Silla in the east, adjoined Goguryeo in the north, and on the southwest were bounded entirely by the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Its borders ran east to Silla, north to Goguryeo, and southwest to the sea on all sides.

sentences.zh: 東西四百五十里，南北九百餘里。

translations.literal: East to west four hundred fifty li; north to south more than nine hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: It measured four hundred fifty li east to west and more than nine hundred li north to south.

sentences.zh: 治固麻城。

translations.literal: The capital was governed from Gumo.
translations.idiomatic: The court sat at Gumo.

sentences.zh: 其外更有五方：中方曰古沙城，東方曰得安城，南方曰久知下城，西方曰刀先城，北方曰熊津城。

translations.literal: Outside there were five further regions: the central region was called Gusa Fortress, the eastern region Deoan Fortress, the southern region Guchihaha Fortress, the western region Doseon Fortress, and the northern region Ungjin Fortress.
translations.idiomatic: Five outer regions surrounded the capital: central Gusa, eastern Deoan, southern Guchihaha, western Doseon, and northern Ungjin.

sentences.zh: 王姓夫餘氏，號於羅瑕，民呼為鞬吉支，夏言竝王也。

translations.literal: The king's surname was Buyeo; his title was Woroja, and the people called him Geonjiji—in Chinese, both mean king.
translations.idiomatic: Kings bore the Buyeo surname and the title Woroja; commoners called them Geonjiji—both mean king in Chinese.

sentences.zh: 妻號於陸，夏言妃也。

translations.literal: The consort's title was Worok—in Chinese, consort.
translations.idiomatic: The queen's title was Worok—consort in Chinese.

sentences.zh: 官有十六品。

translations.literal: Offices had sixteen ranks.
translations.idiomatic: There were sixteen official ranks.

sentences.zh: 左平五人，一品；

translations.literal: Five Left Peaces, first rank;
translations.idiomatic: Five Left Peaces, first rank;

sentences.zh: 達率三十人，二品；

translations.literal: thirty Tolu, second rank;
translations.idiomatic: thirty Tolu, second rank;

sentences.zh: 恩率三品；

translations.literal: Enlu, third rank;
translations.idiomatic: Enlu, third rank;

sentences.zh: 德率四品；

translations.literal: Delu, fourth rank;
translations.idiomatic: Delu, fourth rank;

sentences.zh: 扞率五品；

translations.literal: Hanlu, fifth rank;
translations.idiomatic: Hanlu, fifth rank;

sentences.zh: 柰率六品。

translations.literal: Nailu, sixth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Nailu, sixth rank.

sentences.zh: 六品已上，冠飾銀華。

translations.literal: From the sixth rank upward, caps were adorned with silver flowers.
translations.idiomatic: From the sixth rank up, caps bore silver floral ornaments.

sentences.zh: 將德七品，紫帶；

translations.literal: Jangde, seventh rank, purple belt;
translations.idiomatic: Jangde, seventh rank, purple belt;

sentences.zh: 施德八品，皂帶；

translations.literal: Sideok, eighth rank, black belt;
translations.idiomatic: Sideok, eighth rank, black belt;

sentences.zh: 固德九品，赤帶；

translations.literal: Gokde, ninth rank, red belt;
translations.idiomatic: Gokde, ninth rank, red belt;

translations.literal: (Li)
translations.idiomatic: The character Li here is erroneous; the text below reads Ji.

sentences.zh: 〔季〕德十品，青帶；

translations.literal: [Ji]de, tenth rank, green belt;
translations.idiomatic: Jide, tenth rank, green belt;

sentences.zh: 對德十一品，文督十二品，皆黃帶；

translations.literal: Duide, eleventh rank; Mundok, twelfth rank—both yellow belt;
translations.idiomatic: Duide, eleventh rank; Mundok, twelfth rank—both yellow belt;

sentences.zh: 武督十三品，佐軍十四品，振武十五品，克虞十六品，皆白帶。

translations.literal: Mudok, thirteenth rank; Jogun, fourteenth rank; Jinmu, fifteenth rank; Gyeok, sixteenth rank—all white belt.
translations.idiomatic: Mudok, thirteenth rank; Jogun, fourteenth; Jinmu, fifteenth; Gyeok, sixteenth—all white belt.

sentences.zh: 自恩率以下，官無常員，各有部司，分掌衆務。

translations.literal: From Enlu downward offices had no fixed number of incumbents; each had its own department to divide and administer the multitude of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: From Enlu down, posts had no fixed headcount; each department managed its own affairs.

sentences.zh: 內官有前內部、穀部、肉部、內掠部、外掠部、馬部、刀部、功德部、藥部、木部、法部、後官部。

translations.literal: Inner offices included the Former Inner Department, Grain Department, Meat Department, Inner Plunder Department, Outer Plunder Department, Horse Department, Blade Department, Merit Department, Medicine Department, Wood Department, Law Department, and Rear Consort Department.
translations.idiomatic: Inner bureaus included the Former Inner, Grain, Meat, Inner Plunder, Outer Plunder, Horse, Blade, Merit, Medicine, Wood, Law, and Rear Consort departments.

sentences.zh: 外官有司軍部、司徒部、司空部、司寇部、點口部、客部、外舍部、綢部、日官部、都市部。

translations.literal: Outer offices included the Military Affairs Department, Minister of the Masses Department, Minister of Works Department, Minister of Justice Department, Population Registration Department, Guest Department, Outer Quarters Department, Silk Department, Solar Office Department, and Market Department.
translations.idiomatic: Outer bureaus included Military Affairs, Minister of the Masses, Minister of Works, Minister of Justice, Population Registration, Guest, Outer Quarters, Silk, Solar Office, and Market departments.

sentences.zh: 都下有萬家，分為五部，曰上部、前部、中部、下部、後部，統兵五百人。

translations.literal: Under the capital were ten thousand households, divided into five divisions called Upper, Front, Central, Lower, and Rear, commanding five hundred troops.
translations.idiomatic: The capital district held ten thousand households in five divisions—Upper, Front, Central, Lower, and Rear—each commanding five hundred troops.

sentences.zh: 五方各有方領一人，以達率為之；

translations.literal: Each of the five regions had one regional leader, filled by a Tolu;
translations.idiomatic: Each of the five regions had one regional leader, a Tolu;

sentences.zh: 郡將三人，以德率為之。

translations.literal: Three commandery generals, with Delu filling the post.
translations.idiomatic: Three commandery generals were appointed from the Delu rank.

sentences.zh: 方統兵一千二百人以下，七百人以上。

translations.literal: Each commanded troops from seven hundred up to twelve hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Each commanded between seven hundred and twelve hundred troops.

sentences.zh: 城之內外民庶及餘小城，咸分

translations.literal: The people within and without the cities and the remaining small towns were all divided
translations.idiomatic: Commoners inside and outside the cities and in lesser towns were all assigned

translations.literal: (Xi)
translations.idiomatic: Xi, an erroneous character; see the emended li below.

sentences.zh: 〔隸〕焉。

translations.literal: [Li] to them.
translations.idiomatic: They were registered as subordinates.

sentences.zh: 其衣服，男子畧同於高麗。

translations.literal: Their clothing: men's dress was much the same as Goguryeo's.
translations.idiomatic: Men dressed much like Goguryeo men.

sentences.zh: 若朝拜祭祀，其冠兩廂加翅，戎事則不。

translations.literal: For court audience and sacrifice their caps had wings added on both sides; in military affairs they did not.
translations.idiomatic: For court and sacrifice they wore caps with winged side-panels; not in wartime.

sentences.zh: 拜謁之禮，以兩手據地為敬。

translations.literal: The etiquette of bowing and audience used both hands planted on the ground as respect.
translations.idiomatic: They bowed by placing both hands on the ground.

sentences.zh: 婦人衣

translations.literal: Women's clothing
translations.idiomatic: Women wore

translations.literal: (Yi)
translations.idiomatic: Yi, an erroneous character; see the emended si below.

sentences.zh: 〔似〕袍，而袖微大。

translations.literal: [Si] robes, with sleeves slightly large.
translations.idiomatic: They wore robe-like garments with rather full sleeves.

sentences.zh: 在室者，編發盤於首，後垂一道為飾；

translations.literal: Those indoors braided their hair coiled on the head, with one strand hanging behind as ornament;
translations.idiomatic: Unmarried women braided their hair on the crown with one trailing lock for ornament;

sentences.zh: 出嫁者，乃分為兩道焉。

translations.literal: those who had married then divided it into two strands.
translations.idiomatic: married women divided the braid into two locks.

sentences.zh: 兵有弓箭刀矛。

translations.literal: Weapons included bows, arrows, knives, and spears.
translations.idiomatic: Their arms were bows, arrows, knives, and spears.

sentences.zh: 俗重騎射，兼愛墳史。

translations.literal: Custom prized mounted archery and also loved the histories and annals.
translations.idiomatic: They valued mounted archery and prized historical writing.

sentences.zh: 其秀異者，頗解屬文。

translations.literal: Among their outstanding men, many could compose linked prose.
translations.idiomatic: Talented men among them often mastered literary composition.

sentences.zh: 又解陰陽五行。

translations.literal: They also understood yin-yang and the Five Phases.
translations.idiomatic: They also understood yin-yang lore and the Five Phases.

sentences.zh: 用宋《元嘉曆》，以建寅月為歲首。

translations.literal: They used the Song Yuanjia Calendar, taking the first month of yin as the year's beginning.
translations.idiomatic: They used the Song Yuanjia calendar with the yin month as New Year.

sentences.zh: 亦解醫藥卜筮占相之術。

translations.literal: They also understood medicine, divination by milfoil, and the arts of physiognomy and augury.
translations.idiomatic: They practiced medicine, milfoil divination, physiognomy, and augury.

sentences.zh: 有投壺、樗蒲等雜戲，然尤尚奕棊。

translations.literal: They had miscellaneous games such as pitch-pot and chupu, yet especially honored weiqi.
translations.idiomatic: They played pitch-pot, chupu, and other games, but prized weiqi above all.

sentences.zh: 僧尼寺塔甚多，而無道士。

translations.literal: Buddhist monks and nuns and temple pagodas were very numerous, but there were no Daoist priests.
translations.idiomatic: Monasteries and pagodas were numerous, but there were no Daoist priests.

sentences.zh: 賦稅以布絹絲麻及米等，量歲豐儉，差等輸之。

translations.literal: Taxes were cloth, silk, hemp, and rice, according to the year's abundance or scarcity, paid in graded amounts.
translations.idiomatic: Taxes in cloth, silk, hemp, and rice varied with the harvest year by graded assessment.

sentences.zh: 其刑罰：反叛、退軍及殺人者，斬；

translations.literal: Their punishments: for rebellion, retreat from battle, and murder, beheading;
translations.idiomatic: Penalties: rebels, deserters, and murderers were beheaded;

sentences.zh: 盜者，流，其贓兩倍徵之；

translations.literal: thieves were banished and restitution levied at double the stolen goods;
translations.idiomatic: thieves were exiled and paid double restitution;

sentences.zh: 婦人犯姦者，沒入夫家為婢。

translations.literal: women who committed adultery were confiscated into the husband's household as maidservants.
translations.idiomatic: adulterous women were taken into the husband's house as bondmaids.

sentences.zh: 婚娶之禮，畧同華俗。

translations.literal: Marriage rites were much the same as Central States custom.
translations.idiomatic: Marriage customs largely followed Chinese practice.

sentences.zh: 父母及夫死者，三年治服；

translations.literal: When parents or husbands died, mourning dress was worn for three years;
translations.idiomatic: Parents and husbands were mourned for three years;

sentences.zh: 餘親，則葬訖除之。

translations.literal: for other kin, once burial was complete mourning was removed.
translations.idiomatic: other kin were mourned only until burial was finished.

sentences.zh: 土田下濕，氣候溫暖。

translations.literal: The soil was low and damp; the climate warm.
translations.idiomatic: The land was low and wet, the climate mild.

sentences.zh: 五穀雜果菜蔬及酒醴肴饌藥品之屬，多同於內地。

translations.literal: The five grains, mixed fruits, vegetables, wine, delicacies, and medicinal products mostly resembled those of the inner lands.
translations.idiomatic: Grain, fruit, vegetables, wine, food, and medicines largely matched those of the interior.

sentences.zh: 唯無駝驢騾羊鵝鴨等。

translations.literal: Only camels, donkeys, mules, sheep, geese, ducks, and the like were lacking.
translations.idiomatic: They lacked camels, donkeys, mules, sheep, geese, ducks, and similar stock.

sentences.zh: 其王以四仲之月，祭天及五帝之神。

translations.literal: The king in the four zhong months sacrificed to Heaven and the spirits of the Five Emperors.
translations.idiomatic: In the four seasonal mid-months the king sacrificed to Heaven and the Five Emperors.

sentences.zh: 又每歲四祠其始祖仇台之廟。

translations.literal: He also four times yearly sacrificed at the shrine of the founding ancestor Qiutai.
translations.idiomatic: Four times yearly he sacrificed at the shrine of the founder Qiutai.

sentences.zh: 蠻者，盤瓠之後。

translations.literal: The Man were descendants of Panhu.
translations.idiomatic: The Man traced descent from Panhu.

sentences.zh: 族類

translations.literal: The clans
translations.idiomatic: Their clans

translations.literal: (Fan)
translations.idiomatic: Fan, an erroneous character; see the emended fan proliferate below.

sentences.zh: 〔蕃〕衍，散處江、淮之間，汝、豫之郡。

translations.literal: [Fan] proliferated, scattered between the Yangzi and Huai, in the commanderies of Ru and Yu.
translations.idiomatic: They multiplied and spread between the Yangzi and Huai, across Ru and Yu prefectures.

sentences.zh: 憑險作梗，世為寇亂。

translations.literal: Relying on rugged terrain they made obstruction and through the ages were raiders and rebels.
translations.idiomatic: They used rugged terrain to resist and for generations raided and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 逮魏人失馭，其暴滋甚。

translations.literal: When Wei lost control, their violence grew still worse.
translations.idiomatic: When Northern Wei lost its grip, their violence worsened.

sentences.zh: 有冉氏、向氏、田氏者，陬落尤盛。

translations.literal: There were clans Ran, Xiang, and Tian whose hamlets were especially flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: The Ran, Xiang, and Tian clans had the strongest settlements.

sentences.zh: 餘則大者萬家，小者千戶。

translations.literal: The rest ranged from ten thousand households for the great to a thousand for the small.
translations.idiomatic: Lesser groups held from ten thousand households down to a thousand.

sentences.zh: 更相崇樹，僭稱王侯，屯據三峽，斷遏水路，荊、蜀行人，至有假道者。

translations.literal: They exalted one another in turn, usurping the titles of kings and marquises, holding the Three Gorges and cutting the water routes; travelers of Jing and Shu even had to borrow passage.
translations.idiomatic: They hailed one another as kings and marquises, held the Three Gorges, blocked the waterways, and forced travelers from Jing and Shu to seek passage by leave.

sentences.zh: 太祖畧定伊、瀍，聲教南被，諸蠻畏威，靡然向風矣。

translations.literal: When Taizu briefly settled Yi and Chan, his transforming influence spread south, and the many Man feared his might and turned to the wind like grass.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen secured the Yi and Chan region, his authority spread south and the Man clans submitted in waves.

sentences.zh: 大統五年，蔡陽蠻王魯超明內屬，以為南雍州刺史，仍世襲焉。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Datong, the Caiyang Man king Lu Chaoming submitted inward and was made Governor of Southern Yong Province, the post passing in succession.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong year 5 the Caiyang Man king Lu Chaoming submitted and was made Governor of Southern Yong, an hereditary post.

sentences.zh: 十一年，蠻首梅勒特來貢其方物。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the Man chieftain Meilete came to present local products in tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In year 11 the Man chief Meilete presented tribute.

sentences.zh: 尋而蠻帥田杜清及沔、漢諸蠻擾動，大將軍楊忠擊破之。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the Man leaders Tian Duqing and the Man of Mian and Han stirred trouble, and Grand General Yang Zhong defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Tian Duqing and the Mian and Han Man rebelled; Grand General Yang Zhong defeated them.

sentences.zh: 其後蠻帥杜青和自稱巴州刺史，以州入附。

translations.literal: Later the Man leader Du Qinghe styled himself Governor of Ba Prefecture and submitted the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Man chief Du Qinghe called himself Governor of Ba and surrendered the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 朝廷因其所稱而授之。

translations.literal: The court granted what he called himself and invested him.
translations.idiomatic: The court recognized his title and confirmed the appointment.

sentences.zh: 青和後遂反，攻圍東梁州。

translations.literal: Qinghe later rebelled and besieged Eastern Liang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Qinghe soon rebelled and besieged Eastern Liang.

sentences.zh: 其唐州蠻田魯嘉亦叛，自號豫州伯。

translations.literal: The Tang Prefecture Man Tian Lujia also rebelled and styled himself Earl of Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang Prefecture Man Tian Lujia rebelled and called himself Earl of Yu.

sentences.zh: 王雄、權景宣等前後討平之。

translations.literal: Wang Xiong, Quan Jingxuan, and others in succession suppressed them.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiong, Quan Jingxuan, and others crushed them in turn.

sentences.zh: 語在泉仲遵及景宣傳。

translations.literal: The account is in the biographies of Quan Zhongzun and Jingxuan.
translations.idiomatic: The full account appears in the biographies of Quan Zhongzun and Jingxuan.

sentences.zh: 魏廢帝初，蠻酋樊舍舉落內附，以為淮北三州諸軍事、淮州刺史、淮安郡公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the deposed Emperor of Wei, the Man chieftain Fan She led his settlement inward and was made Commander-in-Chief of the Three Huai North Prefectures, Governor of Huai, and Duke of Huai'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Fei of Wei acceded, the Man chief Fan She submitted and was made commander of the three Huai north prefectures, Huai governor, and Duke of Huai'an.

sentences.zh: 于謹等平江陵，諸蠻騷動，詔豆盧寧、蔡祐等討破之。

translations.literal: When Yu Jin and others pacified Jiangling, the many Man stirred; an edict ordered Dou Lu Ning, Cai You, and others to defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Jin took Jiangling the Man rose; Dou Lu Ning and Cai You were sent to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝二年，蠻酋宜民王田興彥、北荊州刺史梅季昌等相繼款附。

translations.literal: In the second year of Emperor Gong of Wei, the Man chieftains the King of the People Tian Xingyan of Yimin and the Northern Jing Governor Mei Jichang in succession came to offer allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei Gongdi year 2 the Man chiefs King of the People Tian Xingyan and Northern Jing governor Mei Jichang submitted in turn.

sentences.zh: 以興彥、季昌竝為開府儀同三司，加季昌洛州刺史，賜爵石台縣公。

translations.literal: Xingyan and Jichang were both made Peer of Threefold Honours with Opening Office; Jichang was additionally given Luozhou and enfeoffed Duke of Shitai.
translations.idiomatic: Both were made Opening Office, Peer of Threefold Honours; Jichang also received Luozhou and the title Duke of Shitai.

sentences.zh: 其後巴西人譙淹扇動羣蠻，以附於梁。

translations.literal: Later the Ba man Qiao Yan stirred the Man clans to attach to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Ba native Qiao Yan incited the Man to side with Liang.

sentences.zh: 蠻帥向鎮侯、向

translations.literal: The Man leaders Xiang Zhenhou and Xiang
translations.idiomatic: The Man chiefs Xiang Zhenhou and Xiang

translations.literal: (Ri)
translations.idiomatic: Ri, an erroneous character; see the emended Bai below.

sentences.zh: 〔白〕彪等應之。

translations.literal: [Bai] Biao and others responded.
translations.idiomatic: Baibiao and others joined the revolt.

sentences.zh: 向五子王又攻陷信州。

translations.literal: Xiang the Fifth Son King again captured Xin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang the Fifth Son King again took Xin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 田烏度、田都唐等抄斷江路。

translations.literal: Tian Wudu and Tian Dutang and others cut the Yangzi route.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Wudu and Tian Dutang cut the river road.

sentences.zh: 文子榮復據荊州之汶陽郡，自稱仁州刺史。

translations.literal: Wen Zirong again held Wenyang commandery of Jingzhou and styled himself Governor of Ren.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Zirong seized Jingzhou's Wenyang and called himself Governor of Ren.

sentences.zh: 幷鄰州刺史蒲微亦舉兵逆命。

translations.literal: The neighboring prefecture governor Pu Wei also raised troops in defiance.
translations.idiomatic: Neighboring governor Pu Wei also rebelled.

sentences.zh: 詔田弘、賀若敦、潘招、李遷哲討破之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Tian Hong, He Ruo Dun, Pan Zhao, and Li Qianzhe to defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Hong, He Ruo Dun, Pan Zhao, and Li Qianzhe were ordered to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 語在敦及遷哲、

translations.literal: The account is in the biographies of Dun and Qianzhe and
translations.idiomatic: The account is in the biographies of Dun, Qianzhe, and

translations.literal: (Yang)
translations.idiomatic: Yang, an erroneous character; see the emended Yang below.

sentences.zh: 〔陽〕雄等傳。

translations.literal: [Yang] Xiong and others.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xiong.

sentences.zh: 武成初，文州蠻叛，州選軍討定之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wucheng, the Wenzhou Man rebelled; the prefecture chose troops and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wucheng the Wenzhou Man rebelled; local forces pacified them.

sentences.zh: 尋而冉令賢、向五子王等又攻陷白帝，殺開府楊長華，遂相率作亂。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Ran Lingxian, Xiang the Fifth Son King, and others again captured Baidi, killed Opening Office Yang Changhua, and then joined in rebellion together.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Ran Lingxian and Xiang the Fifth Son King took Baidi, killed Yang Changhua, and rose together.

sentences.zh: 前後遣開府元契、趙剛等總兵出討，雖頗剪其族類，而元惡未除。

translations.literal: Opening Office Yuan Qi, Zhao Gang, and others were repeatedly sent with troops to campaign; though they cut down many clans, the chief villain was not removed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Qi and Zhao Gang campaigned repeatedly; many clans were destroyed but the ringleaders remained.

sentences.zh: 天和元年，詔開府陸騰督王亮、司馬裔等討之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianhe, an edict ordered Opening Office Lu Teng to supervise Wang Liang, Sima Yi, and others in the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of  Lu Teng was ordered to command Wang Liang, Sima Yi, and others against them.

sentences.zh: 騰水陸俱進，次于湯口，先遣喻之。

translations.literal: Teng advanced by land and water together and halted at Tangkou, first sending envoys to admonish them.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Teng advanced by land and water to Tangkou and first sent envoys to warn them.

sentences.zh: 而令賢方增浚城池，嚴設扞禦。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Lingxian was deepening moats and walls and setting stern defenses.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Lingxian deepened walls and strengthened defenses.

sentences.zh: 遣其長子西黎、次子南王領其支屬，於江南險要之地置立十城，遠結涔陽蠻為其聲援。

translations.literal: He sent his eldest son Xili and second son the Southern King with their dependents to ten fortified places on the Jiang south's strategic heights, linking far with the Cenyang Man as their support.
translations.idiomatic: He sent sons Xili and the Southern King to ten strongpoints in the south, allying with the Cenyang Man.

sentences.zh: 令賢率其精卒，固守水邏城。

translations.literal: Lingxian himself led his picked troops and held fast at Shuilo Fortress.
translations.idiomatic: Lingxian held Shuilo with his elite troops.

sentences.zh: 騰乃總集將帥，謀其進趣。

translations.literal: Teng then gathered the generals to plan the advance.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Teng gathered his officers to plan the advance.

sentences.zh: 咸欲先取水邏，然後經畧江南。

translations.literal: All wished first to take Shuilo and then deal with the Jiang south.
translations.idiomatic: All favored taking Shuilo first, then the south bank.

sentences.zh: 騰言於衆曰：「令賢內恃水邏金湯之險，外托涔陽輔車之援，兼復資糧充實，器械精新。

translations.literal: Teng said to the assembly: "Lingxian relies within on Shuilo's golden moat and without on Cenyang's chariot-pole support, and moreover his provisions are full and weapons new and fine.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Teng told them: "Lingxian trusts Shuilo's defenses and Cenyang's aid, with full stores and fresh arms.

sentences.zh: 以我懸軍攻其嚴壘，脫一戰不剋，更成其氣。

translations.literal: If we as a suspended army attack his strong fortress and by chance one battle fails, his spirit will only grow.
translations.idiomatic: If our isolated force assaults his fortress and fails once, his morale will rise.

sentences.zh: 不如頓軍湯口，先取江南，剪其羽毛，然後進軍水邏。

translations.literal: Better to halt the army at Tangkou, first take the Jiang south, cut his feathers, and then advance on Shuilo.
translations.idiomatic: Better to hold at Tangkou, take the south bank first, clip his wings, then strike Shuilo.

sentences.zh: 此制勝之計也。」

translations.literal: This is the plan for certain victory."
translations.idiomatic: That is how we win."

sentences.zh: 衆皆然之。

translations.literal: The multitude all approved.
translations.idiomatic: All agreed.

sentences.zh: 乃遣開府王亮率衆渡江，旬日攻拔其八城，凶黨奔散。

translations.literal: He then sent Opening Office Wang Liang with troops across the river; in ten days they stormed eight fortresses and the rebels scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Liang crossed the river and in ten days took eight forts; the rebels fled.

sentences.zh: 獲賊帥冉承公幷生口三千人，降其部衆一千戶。

translations.literal: They captured the bandit leader Ran Chenggong together with three thousand captives and received the submission of a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: They took Ran Chenggong and three thousand captives and accepted a thousand households in surrender.

sentences.zh: 遂簡募驍勇，數道入攻水邏。

translations.literal: Then they selected fierce warriors and attacked Shuilo by several routes.
translations.idiomatic: They then picked elite troops and assaulted Shuilo on several routes.

sentences.zh: 路經石壁城。

translations.literal: The route passed Shibi Fortress.
translations.idiomatic: The march passed Shibi Fortress.

sentences.zh: 此城峻嶮，四面壁立，故以名焉。

translations.literal: This fortress was steep and perilous, with walls standing on all four sides—hence the name.
translations.idiomatic: The fortress was sheer, walled on every side, hence its name.

sentences.zh: 唯有一小路，緣梯而上。

translations.literal: There was only one narrow path, climbing by ladder.
translations.idiomatic: Only one path climbed by ladder.

sentences.zh: 蠻蜑以為峭絕，非兵衆所行。

translations.literal: The Man and boat peoples thought it too sheer for troops to pass.
translations.idiomatic: The Man thought it impassable for an army.

sentences.zh: 騰被甲先登，衆軍繼進，備經危阻，累月乃得舊路。

translations.literal: Teng donned armor and climbed first; the army followed, enduring repeated dangers, and only after months regained the old route.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Teng armored himself and led the climb; the army followed through months of peril.

sentences.zh: 且騰先任隆州總管，雅知蠻帥冉伯犁、冉安西與令賢有隙。

translations.literal: Moreover Teng had earlier served as Commander of Long Prefecture and knew well that the Man leaders Ran Boli and Ran Anxi were at odds with Lingxian.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Teng, former Longzhou commander, knew the Man chiefs Ran Boli and Ran Anxi hated Lingxian.

sentences.zh: 騰乃招誘伯犁等，結為父子，又多遺其金帛。

translations.literal: Teng then enticed Boli and others, binding them as sworn kin, and also sent them much gold and silk.
translations.idiomatic: He won over Boli with gifts and sworn brotherhood.

sentences.zh: 伯犁等悅，遂為鄉導。

translations.literal: Boli and the others were pleased and then served as local guides.
translations.idiomatic: Boli gladly guided the army.

sentences.zh: 水邏側又有石勝城者，亦是險要。

translations.literal: Beside Shuilo there was also Shisheng Fortress, likewise strategic.
translations.idiomatic: Near Shuilo stood Shisheng Fortress, also a strongpoint.

sentences.zh: 令賢使兄子龍真據之。

translations.literal: Lingxian sent his elder brother's son Long Zhen to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: Lingxian put his nephew Long Zhen there.

sentences.zh: 騰又密誘龍真云，若平水邏，使其代令賢處。

translations.literal: Teng also secretly enticed Long Zhen, saying that if Shuilo were pacified he would place him in Lingxian's seat.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Teng secretly promised Long Zhen Lingxian's place if Shuilo fell.

sentences.zh: 龍真大悅，密遣其子詣騰。

translations.literal: Long Zhen was greatly pleased and secretly sent his son to Teng.
translations.idiomatic: Long Zhen sent his son to Lu Teng in secret.

sentences.zh: 騰乃厚加禮接，賜以金帛。

translations.literal: Teng then treated him with generous courtesy and bestowed gold and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Teng received him with honor and gifts of gold and silk.

sentences.zh: 蠻貪利旣深，仍請立效。

translations.literal: The Man, their greed for profit now deep, still asked to pledge achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Greedy for the bounty, the Man asked to prove their loyalty in battle.

sentences.zh: 乃謂騰曰：「欲翻所據城，恐人力寡少。」

translations.literal: He then said to Teng: "I wish to turn the fortress I hold, but fear my manpower is too few."
translations.idiomatic: He told Lu Teng: "I want to turn the fortress I hold, but I lack men."

sentences.zh: 騰許以三百兵助之。

translations.literal: Teng promised three hundred troops to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Teng promised three hundred men to help.

sentences.zh: 旣而遣二千人銜枚夜進。

translations.literal: Presently he sent two thousand men with gags in their mouths advancing by night.
translations.idiomatic: Then he sent two thousand men with gags in their mouths by night.

sentences.zh: 龍真力不能禦，遂平石勝城。

translations.literal: Long Zhen's strength could not resist, and Shisheng Fortress was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Long Zhen could not hold out and Shisheng fell.

sentences.zh: 晨至水邏，蠻衆大潰，斬首萬餘級，虜獲一萬口。

translations.literal: At dawn they reached Shuilo; the Man masses broke in great rout, more than ten thousand heads cut off and ten thousand mouths captured.
translations.idiomatic: By dawn they reached Shuilo; the Man army collapsed with more than ten thousand killed and ten thousand taken.

sentences.zh: 令賢遁走，追而獲之，幷其子弟等皆斬之。

translations.literal: Lingxian fled; pursued and captured, together with his sons and younger kin all were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Lingxian fled, was caught, and was executed with his sons and kin.

sentences.zh: 司馬裔又別下其二十餘城，獲蠻帥冉三公等。

translations.literal: Sima Yi separately reduced more than twenty of their cities and captured the Man leader Ran Sangong and others.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi took twenty-odd cities and captured the Man chief Ran Sangong.

sentences.zh: 騰乃積其骸骨於水邏城側，為京觀。

translations.literal: Teng then heaped their bones beside Shuilo Fortress as a skull mound.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Teng piled their bones beside Shuilo as a victory mound.

sentences.zh: 後蠻蜑望見，輒大號哭。

translations.literal: Later when the Man and boat peoples saw it, they would wail loudly.
translations.idiomatic: When the Man saw the mound they wailed aloud.

sentences.zh: 自此狼戾之心輟矣。

translations.literal: From this their fierce hearts were stilled.
translations.idiomatic: After that their fierce spirit broke.

sentences.zh: 時向五子王據石默城，令其子寶勝據雙城。

translations.literal: At that time Xiang the Fifth Son King held Shimo Fortress and ordered his son Baosheng to hold Shuang Fortress.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang the Fifth Son King held Shimo and sent his son Baosheng to hold Shuang.

sentences.zh: 水邏平後，頻遣喻之，而五子王猶不從命。

translations.literal: After Shuilo was pacified he repeatedly sent envoys to admonish them, yet the Fifth Son King still did not obey.
translations.idiomatic: After Shuilo fell Lu Teng warned them repeatedly, but the Fifth Son King refused.

sentences.zh: 騰又遣王亮屯牢坪，司馬裔屯雙城以圖之。

translations.literal: Teng again sent Wang Liang to encamp at Laoping and Sima Yi to encamp at Shuang to besiege them.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Teng sent Wang Liang to Laoping and Sima Yi to Shuang to besiege them.

sentences.zh: 騰慮雙城孤峭，攻未易拔。

translations.literal: Teng worried that Shuang was isolated and steep and would not be easy to storm.
translations.idiomatic: He feared Shuang was too steep to storm easily.

sentences.zh: 賊若委城奔散，又難追討。

translations.literal: If the bandits abandoned the city and scattered, pursuit would again be hard.
translations.idiomatic: If the rebels fled the city they would be hard to catch.

sentences.zh: 乃令諸軍周回立柵，遏其走路。

translations.literal: He then ordered the armies to encircle with palisades on all sides, blocking their escape routes.
translations.idiomatic: He ringed the forts with palisades to block escape.

sentences.zh: 賊乃大駭。

translations.literal: The bandits were greatly terrified.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels panicked.

sentences.zh: 於是縱兵擊破之，擒五子王于石默，獲寶勝於雙城，悉斬諸向首領，生擒萬餘口。

translations.literal: Thereupon he unleashed the troops to break them; the Fifth Son King was seized at Shimo and Baosheng captured at Shuang; all the Xiang chiefs were beheaded and more than ten thousand taken alive.
translations.idiomatic: His troops broke them, took the Fifth Son King at Shimo and Baosheng at Shuang, executed the Xiang chiefs, and captured ten thousand alive.

sentences.zh: 信州舊治白帝。

translations.literal: Xin Prefecture's old seat was Baidi.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Prefecture had formerly been at Baidi.

sentences.zh: 騰更于劉備故宮城南，八陣之北，臨江岸築城，移置信州。

translations.literal: Teng then south of the former palace of Liu Bei and north of the Eight Formations, on the river bank built a city and moved Xin Prefecture there.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Teng built a new city south of Liu Bei's old palace and north of the Eight Formations and moved Xin Prefecture there.

sentences.zh: 又以巫縣、信陵、秭歸竝是硤中要險，於是築城置防，以為襟帶焉。

translations.literal: He also took Wu, Xinling, and Zigui—all strategic points in the gorges—and built cities and defenses as strategic belts.
translations.idiomatic: He fortified Wu, Xinling, and Zigui in the gorges as strategic strongpoints.

sentences.zh: 天和六年，蠻渠冉祖喜、冉龍驤又反，詔大將軍趙誾討平之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianhe the Man chiefs Ran Zuxi and Ran Longxiang rebelled again; an edict ordered Grand General Zhao Yan to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhe year 6 the Man chiefs Ran Zuxi and Ran Longxiang rebelled; Zhao Yan crushed them.

sentences.zh: 自此羣蠻懾息，不復為寇矣。

translations.literal: From this the Man clans were cowed and quiet and no longer raided.
translations.idiomatic: After that the Man clans were subdued and ceased raiding.

sentences.zh: 獠者，蓋南蠻之別種，自漢中達於邛、笮，川洞之間，在所皆有之。

translations.literal: The Liao were probably a separate branch of the southern Man, from Hanzhong reaching to Qiong and Zuo, in the ravines and caves wherever they were found.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao were a southern Man offshoot spread from Hanzhong to Qiong and Zuo in every mountain valley.

sentences.zh: 俗多不辨姓氏，又無名字，所生男女，唯以長幼次第呼之。

translations.literal: Custom largely did not distinguish surnames, and they had no personal names; sons and daughters born were only called by the order of seniority.
translations.idiomatic: They often had no surnames or personal names and called children only by birth order.

sentences.zh: 其丈夫稱阿謨、阿段，婦人阿夷、阿第之類，皆其語之次第稱謂也。

translations.literal: Men were called Amo, Aduan, women Ayi, Adi and the like—all ordinal terms in their language.
translations.idiomatic: Men were called Amo or Aduan, women Ayi or Adi—ordinal terms in their tongue.

sentences.zh: 喜則羣聚，怒則相殺，雖父子兄弟，亦手刃之。

translations.literal: When pleased they gathered in crowds; when angry they killed one another—even fathers, sons, and brothers hacked with blades.
translations.idiomatic: Joy brought crowds together; anger brought killing—even fathers and sons struck with blades.

sentences.zh: 遞相掠賣，不避親戚。

translations.literal: They sold one another in turn and did not avoid kin.
translations.idiomatic: They sold one another without regard to kinship.

sentences.zh: 被賣者號叫不服，逃竄避之，乃將買人指撝捕逐，若追亡叛，獲便縛之。

translations.literal: The sold cried out and would not submit, fleeing and hiding; then the buyer would point and drive the capture as if chasing a deserter, and once seized they were bound.
translations.idiomatic: Captives fled until buyers hunted them like deserters and bound them.

sentences.zh: 但經被縛者，卽服為賤隸，不敢更稱良矣。

translations.literal: Once bound they submitted as base slaves and dared not again be called free.
translations.idiomatic: Once bound they accepted slavery and never claimed freedom again.

sentences.zh: 俗畏鬼神，尤尚淫祀巫祝，至有賣其昆季妻孥盡者，乃自賣以祭祀焉。

translations.literal: Custom feared ghosts and spirits and especially honored licentious sacrifices and shaman invocations, even to selling brothers, wives, and children entirely, then selling oneself for sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: They feared spirits and lavish shaman rites, sometimes selling kin or even themselves for sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 往往推一酋帥為王，亦不能遠相統攝。

translations.literal: Often they pushed one chieftain as king, yet could not govern one another from afar.
translations.idiomatic: They often hailed a chieftain as king but could not rule one another from afar.

sentences.zh: 自江左及中州遞有巴、蜀，多恃險不賓。

translations.literal: From the Jiang left and the central provinces, as Ba and Shu passed in succession, many relied on rugged terrain and would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: From the lower Yangzi to the heartland, wherever Ba and Shu lay, many held the mountains and refused submission.

sentences.zh: 太祖平梁、益之後，令所在撫慰。

translations.literal: After Taizu pacified Liang and Yi, he ordered local officials to soothe them.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wen pacified Liang and Yi he ordered local officials to pacify them.

sentences.zh: 其與華民雜居者，亦頗從賦役。

translations.literal: Those who mixed with Chinese also largely followed corvée and taxation.
translations.idiomatic: Those living among Chinese often paid taxes and labor service.

sentences.zh: 然天性暴亂，旋至擾動。

translations.literal: Yet by nature they were violent and chaotic, and soon stirred trouble again.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they were violent by nature and soon rebelled again.

sentences.zh: 每歲命隨近州鎮出兵討之，獲其口以充賤隸，謂之為壓獠焉。

translations.literal: Each year nearby prefectures and garrisons were ordered to campaign; captives were taken to fill base slavery—this was called pressing the Liao.
translations.idiomatic: Each year nearby commands campaigned and took captives as slaves—called pressing the Liao.

sentences.zh: 後有商旅往來者，亦資以為貨，公卿逮于民庶之家，有獠口者多矣。

translations.literal: Later traveling merchants also traded in them as goods; from dukes and ministers down to common households, many had Liao slaves.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants traded in them too; noble and common households alike held Liao slaves.

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝三年，陵州木籠獠反，詔開府陸騰討破之，俘斬萬五千人。

translations.literal: In the third year of Emperor Gong of Wei the Lingzhou Mulong Liao rebelled; an edict ordered Opening Office Lu Teng to defeat them, capturing and beheading fifteen thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei Gongdi year 3 the Lingzhou Mulong Liao rebelled; Lu Teng killed or captured fifteen thousand.

sentences.zh: 保定二年，鐵山獠又反，抄斷江路。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoding the Tieshan Liao rebelled again and cut the Yangzi route.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoding year 2 the Tieshan Liao rebelled and cut the river road.

sentences.zh: 陸騰復攻拔其三城，虜獲三千人，降其種三萬落。

translations.literal: Lu Teng again stormed three of their cities, capturing three thousand and receiving the submission of thirty thousand settlements.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Teng took three cities, captured three thousand, and received thirty thousand settlements in surrender.

sentences.zh: 語在《騰傳》。

translations.literal: The account is in the Biography of Teng.
translations.idiomatic: The account is in Lu Teng's biography.

sentences.zh: 天和三年，梁州恆棱獠叛，總管長史趙文表討之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianhe the Hengling Liao of Liang Prefecture rebelled; Chief Clerk Zhao Wenbiao campaigned against them.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhe year 3 the Liangzhou Hengling Liao rebelled; Zhao Wenbiao was sent against them.

sentences.zh: 軍次巴州，文表欲率衆徑進。

translations.literal: The army halted at Ba Prefecture; Wenbiao wished to lead the troops straight forward.
translations.idiomatic: The army stopped at Ba; Wenbiao wanted to advance directly.

sentences.zh: 軍吏等曰：「此獠旅拒日久，部衆甚強。

translations.literal: The military clerks and others said: "These Liao have resisted for a long time and their following is very strong.
translations.idiomatic: His officers said: "These Liao have resisted long and are strong.

sentences.zh: 討之者皆四面攻之，以分其勢。

translations.literal: Those who campaign against them all attack from four sides to divide their strength.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigns usually attack from four sides to divide them.

sentences.zh: 今若大軍直進，不遣奇兵，恐併力於我，未可制勝。」

translations.literal: If the great army advances straight without sending extraordinary troops, I fear they will combine against us and victory may not be assured."
translations.idiomatic: A straight advance without detachments will let them combine against us."

sentences.zh: 文表曰：「往者旣不能制之，今須別為進趣。

translations.literal: Wenbiao said: "In the past we could not control them; now we must take a different advance.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbiao replied: "Past campaigns failed; we need a new approach.

sentences.zh: 若四面遣兵，則獠降走路絕，理當相率以死拒戰。

translations.literal: If we send troops on four sides, the Liao will have no road of surrender and will surely band together to die resisting.
translations.idiomatic: Four armies would leave them no escape and they would fight to the death.

sentences.zh: 如從一道，則吾得示威恩，分遣使人以理曉諭。

translations.literal: If we take one road, then we can show majesty and kindness, sending envoys separately to instruct them with reason.
translations.idiomatic: One road lets us show mercy and send envoys to reason with them.

sentences.zh: 為惡者討之，歸善者撫之。

translations.literal: Those who do evil we campaign against; those who turn to good we soothe.
translations.idiomatic: We punish the wicked and comfort the willing.

sentences.zh: 善惡旣分，易為經畧。

translations.literal: Once good and evil are divided, planning is easy.
translations.idiomatic: Once good and evil are sorted, the rest is easy.

sentences.zh: 事有變通，奈何欲遵前轍也。」

translations.literal: Affairs have flexibility—why follow the old rut?"
translations.idiomatic: Why cling to the old way?"

sentences.zh: 文表遂以此意遍令軍中。

translations.literal: Wenbiao then spread this intent through the whole army.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbiao spread this plan through the army.

sentences.zh: 時有從軍熟獠，多與恆棱親識，卽以實報之。

translations.literal: At that time there were veteran Liao in the army who knew many Hengling men and reported the truth to them.
translations.idiomatic: Liao soldiers in the army warned their kin among the Hengling.

sentences.zh: 恆棱獠相與聚議，猶豫之間，文表軍已至其界。

translations.literal: The Hengling Liao gathered to deliberate, and while they hesitated Wenbiao's army had already reached their border.
translations.idiomatic: While the Hengling debated, Wenbiao's army was already at their border.

sentences.zh: 獠中先有二路，一路稍平，一路極險。

translations.literal: Among the Liao there were first two routes, one somewhat level and one extremely perilous.
translations.idiomatic: Two paths led in—one easier, one very steep.

sentences.zh: 俄有生獠酋帥數人來見文表曰：「我恐官軍不悉山川，請為鄉導。」

translations.literal: Presently several living Liao chieftains came to see Wenbiao and said: "We fear the government troops do not know the mountains and rivers—please serve as guides."
translations.idiomatic: Liao chiefs offered to guide him, claiming the army did not know the terrain.

sentences.zh: 文表謂之曰：「此路寬平，不須導引，卿但先去，好慰諭子弟也。」

translations.literal: Wenbiao said to them: "This road is wide and level and needs no guide; you need only go ahead and comfort your clansmen."
translations.idiomatic: Wenbiao told them the easy road needed no guide and sent them ahead to reassure their people.

sentences.zh: 乃遣之。

translations.literal: He then dismissed them.
translations.idiomatic: He dismissed them.

sentences.zh: 文表謂其衆曰：「向者，獠帥語吾從寬路而行，必當設伏要我。

translations.literal: Wenbiao said to his troops: "Just now the Liao chiefs told me to take the wide road—they will surely set an ambush to await us.
translations.idiomatic: He told his men the chiefs wanted him on the easy road to ambush him.

sentences.zh: 若從險路，出其不虞，獠衆自離散矣。」

translations.literal: If we take the perilous road and catch them unawares, the Liao masses will scatter of themselves."
translations.idiomatic: The steep road would surprise them and they would scatter."

sentences.zh: 於是勒兵從險道進，其有不通之處，隨卽治之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led the army by the perilous route; where it would not pass he repaired it on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: He took the steep path and repaired it where needed.

sentences.zh: 乘高而望，果見其伏兵。

translations.literal: Climbing high to look, he indeed saw their ambush troops.
translations.idiomatic: From a height he saw the ambush.

sentences.zh: 獠旣失計，爭攜妻子，退保險要。

translations.literal: The Liao, having lost their plan, all carried wives and children and retreated to hold strategic heights.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao, outmaneuvered, fled with families to the heights.

sentences.zh: 文表頓軍大蓬山下，示以禍福，遂相率來降。

translations.literal: Wenbiao encamped below Mount Dapeng, showed fortune and calamity, and they then submitted in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbiao camped below Mount Dapeng, showed mercy and threat, and they surrendered.

sentences.zh: 文表皆慰撫之，仍徵其稅租，無敢動者。

translations.literal: Wenbiao all soothed them and also collected their tax grain; none dared stir.
translations.idiomatic: He soothed them, collected taxes, and none rebelled.

sentences.zh: 後除文表為蓬州刺史，又大得獠和。

translations.literal: Later Wenbiao was made Governor of Peng and again won great harmony with the Liao.
translations.idiomatic: He later became governor of Peng and won the Liao's trust.

sentences.zh: 建德初，李暉為梁州總管，諸獠亦竝從附。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiande, Li Hui was Commander of Liang Prefecture and the many Liao also submitted together.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jiande Li Hui commanded Liangzhou and the Liao submitted.

sentences.zh: 然其種類滋蔓，保據岩壑，依林走險，若履平地，雖屢加兵，弗可窮討。

translations.literal: Yet their kind multiplied and spread, holding cliffs and ravines, following forests and running dangers as if treading level ground; though troops were repeatedly sent, they could not be exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they multiplied in the mountains and moved through forests like level ground; repeated campaigns could not root them out.

sentences.zh: 性又無知，殆同禽獸，諸夷之中，最難以道義招懷者也。

translations.literal: Their nature was also ignorant, nearly the same as birds and beasts; among the many Yi they were the hardest to win with reason and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: They were barely human in custom and the hardest of all tribes to win by moral suasion.

sentences.zh: 宕昌羌者，其先蓋三苗之胤。

translations.literal: The Tanchang Qiang: their forebears were probably descendants of the Three Miao.
translations.idiomatic: The Tanchang Qiang traced descent to the Three Miao.

sentences.zh: 周時與庸、蜀、微、盧等八國從武王滅商。

translations.literal: In Zhou times they with Yong, Shu, Wei, Lu and the other eight states followed King Wu to destroy Shang.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhou they joined Yong, Shu, Wei, Lu, and six other states in overthrowing Shang.

sentences.zh: 漢有先零、燒當等，世為邊患。

translations.literal: Under Han there were Xianlian, Shaodang, and others, through the ages a border affliction.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han came Xianlian, Shaodang, and other Qiang who plagued the frontier for generations.

sentences.zh: 其地，東接中華，西通西域，南北數千里。

translations.literal: Their territory east adjoined the Central States and west connected with the Western Regions, several thousand li north and south.
translations.idiomatic: Their lands ran east to China and west to the Western Regions for thousands of li.

sentences.zh: 姓別自為部落，各立酋帥，皆有地分，不相統攝。

translations.literal: Surnames differed and each formed its own tribe, each setting up a chieftain, all with their own territories, not governing one another.
translations.idiomatic: Each clan had its own chieftain and territory and did not rule the others.

sentences.zh: 宕昌卽其一也。

translations.literal: Tanchang was one among them.
translations.idiomatic: Tanchang was one such group.

sentences.zh: 俗皆土著，居有棟宇。

translations.literal: Custom was all settled inhabitants, dwelling in houses with ridgepoles.
translations.idiomatic: They were sedentary and lived in timber houses.

sentences.zh: 其屋織犛牛尾及羖羊毛覆之。

translations.literal: Their houses wove yak tails and sheep and goat hair to cover them.
translations.idiomatic: Roofs were thatched with yak tail and goat wool.

sentences.zh: 國無法令，又無徭賦。

translations.literal: The state had no laws and no corvée or taxation.
translations.idiomatic: They had no written laws or regular taxes.

sentences.zh: 唯征伐之時，乃相屯聚；

translations.literal: Only when campaigning did they gather together;
translations.idiomatic: They assembled only for war;

sentences.zh: 不然，則各事生業，不相往來。

translations.literal: otherwise each pursued his livelihood and they did not visit one another.
translations.idiomatic: otherwise each household farmed apart without contact.

sentences.zh: 皆衣裘褐，牧養犛牛羊豕，以供其食。

translations.literal: All wore fur and felt, herding yaks, cattle, sheep, and pigs for food.
translations.idiomatic: They wore furs, herded yaks, cattle, sheep, and pigs for food.

sentences.zh: 父子伯叔兄弟死者，卽以其繼母、世叔母、及嫂

translations.literal: When fathers, uncles, and brothers died, they then took their stepmothers, uncles' wives, and sisters-in-law
translations.idiomatic: When fathers, uncles, or brothers died, they took stepmothers, uncles' wives, and sisters-in-law

sentences.zh: （姊妹）

translations.literal: (Sisters)
translations.idiomatic: Sisters, an erroneous character; see the emended brothers' wives below.

sentences.zh: 〔弟婦〕等為妻。

translations.literal: [Brothers' wives] and the like as wives.
translations.idiomatic: They also took brothers' wives as wives.

sentences.zh: 俗無文字，但候草木榮落，以記歲時。

translations.literal: Custom had no writing but only watched plants flourish and wither to mark the seasons.
translations.idiomatic: They had no writing and marked seasons by plants' growth and decay.

sentences.zh: 三年一相聚，殺牛羊以祭天。

translations.literal: Every three years they gathered once, killing cattle and sheep to sacrifice to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Every three years they gathered to sacrifice cattle and sheep to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 有梁

translations.literal: There was a Liang
translations.idiomatic: A Liang clan

translations.literal: (Le)
translations.idiomatic: Le, an erroneous character; see the emended Qin below.

sentences.zh: 〔勤〕者，世為酋帥，得羌豪心，乃自稱王焉。

translations.literal: [Qin] clan that for generations were chieftains, winning the Qiang nobles' hearts, and styled themselves kings.
translations.idiomatic: Qin clan had long been chieftains, won the Qiang chiefs' loyalty, and called themselves kings.

sentences.zh: 其界自仇池以西，東西千里，

translations.literal: Their borders from west of Chouchi were a thousand li east and west,
translations.idiomatic: Their realm stretched a thousand li east and west from west of Chou Pool,

translations.literal: (Dai)
translations.idiomatic: Dai, an erroneous character; see the emended Xi below.

sentences.zh: 〔席〕水以南，南北八百里。

translations.literal: [Xi] River south, eight hundred li north and south.
translations.idiomatic: Their realm extended eight hundred li north and south from the Xi River.

sentences.zh: 地多山阜，部衆二萬餘落。

translations.literal: The land was mostly mountains and mounds; settlements numbered more than twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The land was mountainous with more than twenty thousand settlements.

sentences.zh: 勤孫彌忽，始通使於後魏。

translations.literal: Qin's grandson Mihuo first sent envoys to the Later Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Qin's grandson Mihuo first sent envoys to Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 太武因其所稱而授之。

translations.literal: Emperor Taiwu according to what they called themselves granted investiture.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu invested them under the titles they claimed.

sentences.zh: 自彌忽至仚定九世，每修職貢不絕。

translations.literal: From Mihuo to Xianding for nine generations, tribute and service were unbroken.
translations.idiomatic: For nine generations from Mihuo to Xianding they paid tribute without fail.

sentences.zh: 後見兩魏分隔，遂懷背誕。

translations.literal: Later, seeing the two Wei divided, they harbored treacherous thoughts.
translations.idiomatic: When the two Wei states split they turned disloyal.

sentences.zh: 永熙末，仚定乃引吐谷渾寇金城。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongxi, Xianding then led Tuyuhun to raid Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Yongxi, Xianding led Tuyuhun to raid Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 大統初，又率其種人入寇。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Datong he again led his tribesmen in to raid.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Datong he raided again with his tribes.

sentences.zh: 詔行臺趙貴督儀同侯莫陳順等擊破之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Mobile Corps Zhao Gui to supervise Peer of Threefold Honours Hou Mo Chen Shun and others to defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Gui and Hou Mo Chen Shun were ordered to defeat them.

sentences.zh: 仚定懼，稱藩請罪。

translations.literal: Xianding was afraid and declared himself a vassal, begging pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Xianding submitted and begged forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 太祖捨之，拜撫軍將軍。

translations.literal: Taizu spared him and appointed him Pacification Army General.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen spared him and made him Pacification Army General.

sentences.zh: 四年，以仚定為南洮州刺史、要安蕃王。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Xianding was made Governor of Southern Tao Prefecture and King of the Yao'an Fan.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he became Southern Tao governor and King of Yao'an Fan.

sentences.zh: 後改洮州為岷州，仍以仚定為刺史。

translations.literal: Later Tao Prefecture was changed to Min Prefecture and Xianding remained governor.
translations.idiomatic: Tao was renamed Min and he kept the governorship.

sentences.zh: 是歲，秦州濁水羌反，州軍討平之。

translations.literal: That year the Zhuoshui Qiang of Qin Prefecture rebelled and the prefectural army pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Qinzhou Zhuoshui Qiang rebelled and were suppressed.

sentences.zh: 七年，仚定又舉兵入寇。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Xianding again raised troops and raided inward.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 Xianding raided again.

sentences.zh: 獨孤信時鎮隴右，詔信率衆便討之。

translations.literal: Dugu Xin then garrisoned Longyou; an edict ordered Xin to lead troops at once to campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Dugu Xin commanded Longyou and was sent to campaign.

sentences.zh: 軍未至而仚定為其下所殺。

translations.literal: Before the army arrived Xianding was killed by his subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Before the army arrived his men killed him.

sentences.zh: 信進兵破其餘黨。

translations.literal: Xin advanced and broke the remaining factions.
translations.idiomatic: Dugu Xin destroyed the remnant rebels.

sentences.zh: 朝廷方欲招懷殊俗，乃更以其弟彌定為宕昌王。

translations.literal: The court wished to win over distant peoples and therefore made his younger brother Mideng Tanchang King.
translations.idiomatic: The court then made his brother Mideng King of Tanchang.

sentences.zh: 十六年，彌定宗人獠甘襲奪其位，彌定來奔。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year Mideng's clansman the Liao Gan seized his position and Mideng fled to submit.
translations.idiomatic: In year 16 the Liao Gan seized his throne and Mideng fled to court.

sentences.zh: 先是，羌酋傍乞鐵匆等因仚定反叛之際，遂擁衆據渠林川，與渭州民鄭五醜扇動諸羌，阻兵逆命。

translations.literal: Earlier the Qiang chieftains Bangqi Tieceng and others, taking advantage of Xianding's rebellion, then gathered their following and held Qulin River, with the Weizhou man Zheng Wuchou stirring the many Qiang to block troops and defy orders.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Qiang chiefs had seized Qulin Valley during Xianding's revolt with Zheng Wuchou stirring the Qiang.

sentences.zh: 至是詔大將軍宇文貴、豆盧寧、涼州刺史史寧等率兵討獠甘等，竝擒斬之，納彌定而還。

translations.literal: At this time an edict ordered Grand General Yuwen Gui, Dou Lu Ning, Liang Prefecture Governor Shi Ning, and others to lead troops against the Liao Gan and others; all were captured and beheaded, Mideng was installed, and they returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Gui and others defeated the Liao Gan, executed the ringleaders, and restored Mideng.

sentences.zh: 語在貴等傳。

translations.literal: The account is in the biographies of Gui and others.
translations.idiomatic: The account is in Yuwen Gui's biography.

sentences.zh: 其後羌酋東念姐、鞏廉俱和等反，大將軍豆盧寧、王勇等前後討平之。

translations.literal: Later the Qiang chieftains Dong Nianjie, Gong Lian, Juhe, and others rebelled; Grand Generals Dou Lu Ning and Wang Yong suppressed them in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Later Qiang chiefs Dong Nianjie and Gong Lian rebelled; Dou Lu Ning and Wang Yong suppressed them.

sentences.zh: 保定初，彌定遣使獻方物。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoding, Mideng sent envoys presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Baoding Mideng sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 三年，又遣使獻生猛獸。

translations.literal: In the third year he again sent envoys presenting live fierce beasts.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he sent live wild beasts as tribute.

sentences.zh: 四年，彌定寇洮州，總管李賢擊走之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Mideng raided Min Prefecture and Commander Li Xian drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 Mideng raided Min; Li Xian repulsed him.

sentences.zh: 是歲，彌定又引吐谷渾寇石門戍，賢復破之。

translations.literal: That year Mideng again led Tuyuhun to raid Shimen garrison and Xian again defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: That year he brought Tuyuhun against Shimen; Li Xian defeated them again.

sentences.zh: 高祖怒，詔大將軍田弘討滅之，以其地為宕州。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu was angry and ordered Grand General Tian Hong to campaign and destroy them, making their land Tan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu ordered Tian Hong to destroy them and made the land Tan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 鄧至羌者，羌之別種也。

translations.literal: The Dengzhi Qiang were a separate branch of the Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: The Dengzhi Qiang were a Qiang offshoot.

sentences.zh: 有像舒治者，世為白水酋帥，自稱王焉。

translations.literal: There was Xiang Shuzhi, for generations chieftain of Baishui, who styled himself king.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Shuzhi's line ruled Baishui and called themselves kings.

sentences.zh: 其地北與宕昌相接，風俗物產亦與宕昌畧同。

translations.literal: Their territory north adjoined Tanchang; customs and products were also much the same as Tanchang.
translations.idiomatic: North they bordered Tanchang; customs matched Tanchang's.

sentences.zh: 自舒治至簷桁十一世。

translations.literal: From Shuzhi to Yanheng was eleven generations.
translations.idiomatic: Eleven generations passed from Shuzhi to Yanheng.

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝元年，簷桁失國來奔，太祖令章武公導率兵送復之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Emperor Gong of Wei, Yanheng lost his state and fled to submit; Taizu ordered Duke Zhangwu Dao to lead troops and escort him back.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wei Gongdi Yanheng fled to court; Duke Dao restored him by force.

sentences.zh: 白蘭者，羌之別種也。

translations.literal: Bailan were a separate branch of the Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: The Bailan were another Qiang branch.

sentences.zh: 其地東北接吐谷渾，西北至利模徒，南界那鄂，風俗物產與宕昌畧同。

translations.literal: Their territory northeast adjoined Tuyuhun and northwest reached Limotu; south the border was Na'e; customs and products were much the same as Tanchang.
translations.idiomatic: They bordered Tuyuhun northeast, reached Limotu northwest, and Na'e south.

sentences.zh: 保定元年，遣使獻犀甲鐵鎧。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoding they sent envoys presenting rhinoceros-hide armor and iron mail.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of  they sent rhinoceros armor and iron mail.

sentences.zh: 氐者，西夷之別種。

translations.literal: The Di were a separate branch of the western Yi.
translations.idiomatic: The Di were a western Yi offshoot.

sentences.zh: 三代之際，蓋自有君長，而世一朝見。

translations.literal: In the Three Dynasties era they probably had their own rulers and each generation paid court once.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity they had their own rulers who came to court each generation.

sentences.zh: 故《詩》稱「自彼氐、羌，莫敢不來王」也。
