translations.literal: Therefore the Odes say: "From those Di and Qiang, none dared not come to court."
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Odes: "From those Di and Qiang, none dared fail to come to court."

sentences.zh: 漢武帝滅之，以其地為武都郡。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Han destroyed them and made their land Wudu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Han Wudi conquered them and made Wudu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 自汧、渭抵於巴、蜀，種類實繁。

translations.literal: From Qian and Wei to Ba and Shu the kinds were truly numerous.
translations.idiomatic: From Qian and Wei to Ba and Shu their clans were countless.

sentences.zh: 漢末，有氐帥楊駒，始據仇池百頃，最為彊族。

translations.literal: At the end of Han there was the Di chieftain Yang Ju, who first held a hundred qing at Chou Pool and was the strongest clan.
translations.idiomatic: Late Han Di chief Yang Ju held Chou Pool and became the strongest clan.

sentences.zh: 其後漸盛，乃自稱王。

translations.literal: Later they gradually grew powerful and styled themselves kings.
translations.idiomatic: They grew powerful and called themselves kings.

sentences.zh: 至裔孫纂，為

translations.literal: When descendant Zuan reached his time, he was
translations.idiomatic: Descendant Zuan was

translations.literal: (Fu)
translations.idiomatic: Fu, an erroneous character; see the emended Fu below.

sentences.zh: 〔苻〕堅所滅。

translations.literal: [Fu] Jian who destroyed him.
translations.idiomatic: He was destroyed by Fu Jian.

sentences.zh: 堅敗，其族人定又自稱王。

translations.literal: When Jian was defeated, his clansman Ding again styled himself king.
translations.idiomatic: After Jian's fall his kinsman Ding again called himself king.

sentences.zh: 定為乞伏乾歸所殺。

translations.literal: Ding was killed by Qifu Gangui.
translations.idiomatic: Ding was killed by Qifu Gangui.

sentences.zh: 定從弟盛，代有其國。

translations.literal: Ding's younger cousin Sheng succeeded to their state.
translations.idiomatic: Cousin Sheng took the throne.

sentences.zh: 世受魏氏封拜，亦通使於江左。

translations.literal: For generations they received Wei investiture and also sent envoys to the Jiang left.
translations.idiomatic: They received Wei titles and also sent envoys to the southern courts.

sentences.zh: 然其種落分散，叛服不恆，隴、漢之間，屢被其害。

translations.literal: Yet their clans were scattered, submitting and rebelling without constancy, and between Long and Han they were repeatedly harmed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet clans scattered, rebelled and submitted by turns, and plagued Long and Han.

sentences.zh: 盛之苗裔曰集始，魏封為武興王。

translations.literal: Sheng's descendant was Jishi; Wei enfeoffed him King of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng's descendant Jishi was enfeoffed King of Wuxing by Wei.

sentences.zh: 集始死，子紹先立，遂僭稱大號。

translations.literal: When Jishi died his son Shaoxian succeeded and then usurped the great title.
translations.idiomatic: Jishi's son Shaoxian usurped imperial title.

sentences.zh: 魏將傅豎眼滅之，執紹先歸諸京師，以其地為武興鎮。

translations.literal: Wei general Fu Shuyan destroyed them, seized Shaoxian and took him to the capital, making the land Wuxing Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Shuyan destroyed them, took Shaoxian to the capital, and made Wuxing a garrison.

sentences.zh: 魏氏洛京未定，天下亂，紹先奔還武興，復自立為王。

translations.literal: When Wei's Luoyang was not yet settled and the realm was chaotic, Shaoxian fled back to Wuxing and again set himself up as king.
translations.idiomatic: When Luoyang fell into chaos Shaoxian fled home and made himself king again.

sentences.zh: 太祖定秦、隴，紹先稱藩，送妻子為質。

translations.literal: When Taizu pacified Qin and Long, Shaoxian declared himself a vassal and sent wife and children as hostages.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen took Qin and Long, Shaoxian submitted hostages.

sentences.zh: 大統元年，紹先請其妻女，太祖奏魏帝還之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Datong Shaoxian asked for his wife and daughters; Taizu memorialized the Wei Emperor to return them.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of  he asked for his family back and the emperor returned them.

sentences.zh: 紹先死，子辟邪立。

translations.literal: When Shaoxian died his son Bixie succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoxian's son Bixie succeeded.

sentences.zh: 四年，南岐州氐苻安壽反，攻陷武都，自號太白王。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the Southern Qi Prefecture Di Fu Anshou rebelled, stormed Wudu, and styled himself King of Taibai.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 the Di Fu Anshou took Wudu and called himself King of Taibai.

sentences.zh: 詔大都督侯莫陳順與渭州刺史長孫澄討破之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Grand Commander Hou Mo Chen Shun and Weizhou Governor Zhangsun Cheng to campaign and defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Mo Chen Shun and Zhangsun Cheng defeated him.

sentences.zh: 安壽以其衆降。

translations.literal: Anshou submitted with his following.
translations.idiomatic: Anshou surrendered with his followers.

sentences.zh: 九年，清水氐酋李鼠仁據險作亂，氐帥梁道顯叛攻南由，太祖遣典簽趙昶慰諭之，鼠仁等相繼歸附。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the Qingshui Di chieftain Li Shuren held rugged terrain and made disorder; the Di chief Liang Daoxian rebelled and attacked Nanyou; Taizu sent Registrar Zhao Chang to soothe them and Shuren and others submitted in succession.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9 Li Shuren and Liang Daoxian rebelled; Zhao Chang won them back.

sentences.zh: 語在《昶傳》。

translations.literal: The account is in the Biography of Chang.
translations.idiomatic: The account is in Zhao Chang's biography.

sentences.zh: 十一年，於武興置東益州，以辟邪為刺史。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Eastern Yi Province was established at Wuxing with Bixie as governor.
translations.idiomatic: In year 11 Eastern Yi Province was set at Wuxing with Bixie as governor.

sentences.zh: 十五年，安夷氐復叛，趙昶時為郡守，收其首逆者二十餘人斬之，餘衆乃定。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year the Anyi Di rebelled again; Zhao Chang was then prefect and seized more than twenty ringleaders and beheaded them, and the rest were settled.
translations.idiomatic: In year 15 the Anyi Di rebelled; Zhao Chang executed twenty ringleaders and pacified the rest.

sentences.zh: 於是以昶行南秦州事。

translations.literal: Thereupon Chang was made to act for Southern Qin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chang was then put in charge of Southern Qin.

sentences.zh: 氐帥蓋鬧等相率作亂，鬧據北穀，其党覃洛聚洮中，楊興德、苻雙圍平氐城，姜樊噲亂武階，西結宕昌羌獠甘，共推蓋鬧為主。

translations.literal: The Di chieftain Gai Nao and others rose together in disorder; Nao held Beigu, his party Tan Luo gathered in Tao middle, Yang Xingde and Fu Shuang besieged Pingdi City, Jiang Fanhuai troubled Wujie, west linking with the Tanchang Qiang and the Liao Gan, together pushing Gai Nao as leader.
translations.idiomatic: Di chief Gai Nao rebelled with allies across the region and made Nao their leader.

sentences.zh: 昶分道遣使宣示禍福，然後出兵討之，擒蓋鬧，散其餘黨。

translations.literal: Chang sent envoys by separate routes to proclaim fortune and calamity, then led troops to campaign, captured Gai Nao, and scattered the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Chang warned them, then captured Gai Nao and scattered his followers.

sentences.zh: 興州叛氐復侵逼南岐州，刺史叱羅協遣使告急，昶率兵赴救，又大破之。

translations.literal: Rebel Di of Xing Prefecture again pressed Southern Qi Prefecture; Governor Chiluo Xie sent envoys in emergency and Chang led troops to the rescue and again inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzhou rebels pressed Southern Qi; Zhao Chang relieved and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝末，武興氐反，圍利州。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Gong of Wei the Wuxing Di rebelled and besieged Li Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Wei Gongdi the Wuxing Di besieged Li Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 鳳州固道氐魏天王等亦聚衆回應。

translations.literal: The Gudao Di of Feng Prefecture Wei Tianwang and others also gathered crowds in response.
translations.idiomatic: Fengzhou Di under Wei Tianwang joined the revolt.

sentences.zh: 大將軍豆盧寧等討平之。

translations.literal: Grand General Dou Lu Ning and others suppressed them.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Lu Ning suppressed them.

sentences.zh: 世宗時，興州人〔段〕吒及下辯、栢樹二縣民反，相率破蘭皋戍。

translations.literal: Under Shizong, the Xingzhou man Duan Tuo and the people of Xiabian and Baishu counties rebelled, together storming Langao garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ming, Duan Tuo and county rebels took Langao garrison.

sentences.zh: 氐酋薑多復率廚中氐、蜀攻陷落叢郡以應之。

translations.literal: The Di chieftain Jiang Duo again led the Chuzhong Di and Shu to storm Luocong commandery in support.
translations.idiomatic: Di chief Jiang Duo joined the attack on Luocong.

sentences.zh: 趙昶率衆討平二縣，並斬段吒。

translations.literal: Zhao Chang led troops to pacify the two counties and also beheaded Duan Tuo.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Chang pacified the counties and killed Duan Tuo.

sentences.zh: 而陰平、盧北二郡氐復往往屯聚，與廚中相應。

translations.literal: Yet the Di of Yinping and Lubai commanderies again gathered in many places, responding with the Chuzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Di in Yinping and Lubai rose again in concert.

sentences.zh: 昶乃簡擇精騎，出其不意，徑入廚中。

translations.literal: Chang then chose picked cavalry, took them unawares, and entered Chuzhong directly.
translations.idiomatic: Chang took elite cavalry straight into Chuzhong by surprise.

sentences.zh: 至大竹坪，連破七柵，誅其渠率，二郡竝降。

translations.literal: Reaching Dazhuping he stormed seven stockades in succession, executed their chiefs, and both commanderies submitted.
translations.idiomatic: At Dazhuping he took seven stockades, killed the chiefs, and both commanderies surrendered.

sentences.zh: 及昶還，廚中主氐復為寇掠。

translations.literal: When Chang returned the Chuzhong chief Di again raided and plundered.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang left, Chuzhong Di raided again.

sentences.zh: 昶又遣儀同劉崇義、宇文琦率兵入廚中討之，大破氐衆，斬薑多及苻肆王等。

translations.literal: Chang again sent Peer of Threefold Honours Liu Chongyi and Yuwen Qi to lead troops into Chuzhong to campaign; they inflicted a great defeat on the Di masses and beheaded Jiang Duo and Fu Siwang and others.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Liu Chongyi and Yuwen Qi, who crushed the Di and killed Jiang Duo.

sentences.zh: 於是羣氐竝平。

translations.literal: Thereupon the many Di were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The Di were pacified.

sentences.zh: 及王謙舉兵，沙州氐帥開府楊永安又據州應謙，大將軍達奚儒討平之。

translations.literal: When Wang Qian raised troops, the Shazhou Di chieftain Opening Office Yang Yong'an again held the prefecture in response to Qian; Grand General Daxi Ru suppressed them.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Qian rebelled, Yang Yong'an held Shazhou; Daxi Ru suppressed him.

sentences.zh: 稽胡一曰步落稽，蓋匈奴別種，劉元海五部之苗裔也。

translations.literal: The Jihu, also called Buluoji, were probably a separate branch of the Xiongnu, descendants of Liu Yuanhai's five tribes.
translations.idiomatic: The Jihu, or Buluoji, were likely a Xiongnu offshoot from Liu Yuanhai's five tribes.

sentences.zh: 或云山戎赤狄之後。

translations.literal: Some say they were descendants of the Mountain Rong and Red Di.
translations.idiomatic: Others say they descended from the Mountain Rong and Red Di.

sentences.zh: 自離石以西，安定以東，方七八百里，居山谷間，種落繁熾。

translations.literal: From west of Lishi to east of Anding, about seven or eight hundred li square, they dwelt in mountain valleys and their tribes flourished.
translations.idiomatic: From Lishi west to Anding east they filled valleys across seven or eight hundred li.

sentences.zh: 其俗土著，亦知種田。

translations.literal: Their custom was settled dwelling and they also knew how to plant fields.
translations.idiomatic: They were sedentary and farmed.

sentences.zh: 地少桑蠶，多麻布。

translations.literal: The land had little mulberry and silkworms and much hemp cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Silk was scarce; they wore hemp.

sentences.zh: 其丈夫衣服及死亡殯葬，與中夏畧同。

translations.literal: Men's clothing and death and burial were much the same as the Central States.
translations.idiomatic: Men's dress and funeral rites resembled Chinese practice.

sentences.zh: 婦人則多貫蜃貝以為耳及頸飾。

translations.literal: Women mostly strung cowrie shells as ear and neck ornaments.
translations.idiomatic: Women wore cowrie shells on ears and necks.

sentences.zh: 又與華民錯居，其渠帥頗識文字。

translations.literal: They also mixed with Chinese and their chiefs knew some writing.
translations.idiomatic: Mixed with Chinese, their chiefs often knew writing.

sentences.zh: 然語類夷狄，因譯乃通。

translations.literal: Yet their speech was like the Yi and Di and communication required interpreters.
translations.idiomatic: Their speech was barbarian and needed interpreters.

sentences.zh: 蹲踞無禮，貪而忍害。

translations.literal: They squatted without ritual, greedy and cruel.
translations.idiomatic: They squatted without manners, greedy and cruel.

sentences.zh: 俗好淫穢，處女尤甚。

translations.literal: Custom favored licentiousness; maidens especially so.
translations.idiomatic: Licentiousness was common, especially among maidens.

sentences.zh: 將嫁之夕，方與淫者敘離，夫氏聞之，以多為貴。

translations.literal: On the eve of marriage they still took leave of licentious partners, and the husband's clan heard of it—the more the more honored.
translations.idiomatic: Brides slept with lovers on the eve of marriage; husbands prized a long list of partners.

sentences.zh: 旣嫁之後，頗亦防閑，有犯姦者，隨事懲罰。

translations.literal: After marriage they were somewhat guarded; if adultery occurred punishment followed the case.
translations.idiomatic: After marriage they were watched; adultery was punished.

sentences.zh: 又兄弟死，皆納其妻。

translations.literal: Also when brothers died they all took the wives.
translations.idiomatic: They took brothers' widows in levirate marriage.

sentences.zh: 雖分統郡縣，列於編戶，然輕其徭賦，有異齊民。

translations.literal: Although they were distributed through commanderies and counties and entered the household registers, corvée and taxation were lightened, differing from equal subjects.
translations.idiomatic: Though registered in counties, their taxes were lighter than ordinary subjects'.

sentences.zh: 山谷阻深者，又未盡役屬。

translations.literal: Those in deep mountain barriers were also not fully subject to service.
translations.idiomatic: Deep valleys were not fully taxed or drafted.

sentences.zh: 而凶悍恃險，數為寇亂。

translations.literal: Yet fierce and brutal, relying on terrain, they repeatedly raided and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Fierce and terrain-wise, they raided repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 居河西者，多恃險不賓。

translations.literal: Those dwelling west of the river mostly relied on rugged terrain and would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: West-of-river Jihu often held the mountains and refused submission.

sentences.zh: 時方與齊神武爭衡，未遑經畧。

translations.literal: At the time they were contending with Qi Shenwu and had no leisure for planning.
translations.idiomatic: The court was fighting Qi Shenwu and could not attend to them.

sentences.zh: 太祖乃遣黃門郎楊

translations.literal: Taizu then sent Yellow Gate Gentleman Yang
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen sent Yellow Gate Gentleman Yang

translations.literal: (Zhong)
translations.idiomatic: Zhong, an erroneous character; see the emended Biao below.

sentences.zh: 〔摽〕就安撫之。

translations.literal: [Biao] to go and soothe them.
translations.idiomatic: Biao to pacify them.

sentences.zh: 五年，黑水部衆先叛。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the masses of the Black Water division rebelled first.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 the Black Water division rebelled first.

sentences.zh: 七年，別帥夏州刺史劉平伏又據上郡反。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the separate commander Xia Prefecture Governor Liu Pingfu again held Shang commandery and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 Liu Pingfu of Xiazhou held Shang and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 自是北山諸部，連歲寇暴。

translations.literal: From this the many divisions of the northern mountains raided and plundered year after year.
translations.idiomatic: Northern tribes then raided year after year.

sentences.zh: 太祖前後遣李遠、于謹、侯莫陳崇、李弼等相繼討平之。

translations.literal: Taizu repeatedly sent Li Yuan, Yu Jin, Hou Mo Chen Chong, Li Bi, and others in succession to campaign and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen sent Li Yuan, Yu Jin, Hou Mo Chen Chong, and Li Bi in turn to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 武成初，延州稽胡郝阿保、郝狼皮率其種人附於齊氏。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wucheng the Yanzhou Jihu Hao Abao and Hao Langpi led their tribes to attach to the Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wucheng Yanzhou Jihu Hao Abao and Hao Langpi sided with Northern Qi.

sentences.zh: 阿保自署丞相，狼皮自署柱國，幷與其別部劉桑德共為影響。

translations.literal: Abao styled himself Chancellor and Langpi styled himself Pillar of State; together with their separate division Liu Sangde they acted in mutual support.
translations.idiomatic: Abao called himself Chancellor, Langpi Pillar of State, and allied with Liu Sangde.

sentences.zh: 柱國豆盧寧督諸軍與延州刺史高琳擊破之。

translations.literal: Pillar of State Dou Lu Ning commanded the armies with Yanzhou Governor Gao Lin and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Lu Ning and Gao Lin defeated them.

sentences.zh: 二年，狼皮等餘黨復叛。

translations.literal: In the second year Langpi and the remaining factions rebelled again.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 Langpi's remnant rebelled again.

sentences.zh: 詔大將軍韓

translations.literal: An edict ordered Grand General Han
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Han

translations.literal: (Gao)
translations.idiomatic: Gao, an erroneous character; see the emended Guo below.

sentences.zh: 〔果〕討之，俘斬甚衆。

translations.literal: [Guo] to campaign against them; captives killed and beheaded were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Guo campaigned and killed or captured many.

sentences.zh: 保定中，離石生胡數寇汾北，勳州刺史韋孝寬於險要築城，置兵糧，以遏其路。

translations.literal: In Baoding the Lishi Sheng Hu repeatedly raided north of Fen; Xun Prefecture Governor Wei Xiaokuan built a city at a strategic point and set troops and grain to block their route.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoding Lishi Hu raided north of Fen; Wei Xiaokuan fortified a choke point.

sentences.zh: 及楊忠與突厥伐齊，稽胡等復懷旅拒，不供糧餼。

translations.literal: When Yang Zhong with the Turks campaigned against Qi, the Jihu and others again harbored resistance and would not supply provisions.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Zhong marched with the Turks, Jihu refused supplies.

sentences.zh: 忠乃詐其酋帥，雲與突厥欲回兵討之。

translations.literal: Zhong then deceived their chieftains, saying he and the Turks would turn back to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhong tricked the chiefs, saying the Turks would turn to attack them.

sentences.zh: 酋帥等懼，乃相率供饋焉。

translations.literal: The chieftains were afraid and then submitted supplies in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, the chiefs supplied his army.

sentences.zh: 語在《忠傳》。

translations.literal: The account is in the Biography of Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: The account is in Yang Zhong's biography.

sentences.zh: 其後丹州、綏州、銀州等部內諸胡，與蒲川別帥郝三郎等又頻年逆命。

translations.literal: Later the many Hu within Dan, Sui, and Yin prefectures and others, with the Puchuan separate commander Hao Sanlang and others, for successive years defied orders.
translations.idiomatic: Later Hu in Dan, Sui, and Yin prefectures rebelled with Hao Sanlang.

sentences.zh: 復詔達奚震、辛威、於寔等前後窮討，散其種落。

translations.literal: Again edicts ordered Daxi Zhen, Xin Wei, Yu Shi, and others in succession to pursue to the end and scatter their tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Daxi Zhen, Xin Wei, and Yu Shi were sent to scatter their tribes.

sentences.zh: 天和二年，延州總管宇文盛率衆城銀州，稽胡白鬱久同、喬是羅等欲邀襲盛軍，盛竝討斬之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianhe Yanzhou Commander Yuwen Sheng led crowds to wall Yin Prefecture; the Jihu Bai Yujiu and Qiao Shiruo and others wished to intercept and strike Sheng's army; Sheng together campaigned and beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhe year 2 Yuwen Sheng built Yinzhou; Jihu chiefs who ambushed him were killed.

sentences.zh: 又破其別帥喬三勿同等。

translations.literal: He also defeated their separate commander Qiao Sanwu and others.
translations.idiomatic: He also defeated Qiao Sanwu.

sentences.zh: 五年，開府劉雄出綏州，巡檢北邊，川路稽胡帥喬白郎、喬素勿同等度河逆戰，雄復破之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Opening Office Liu Xiong went out from Suizhou to inspect the northern border; the Jihu chiefs along the river Qiao Bailang, Qiao Suwu, and others crossed the river to fight in opposition and Xiong again defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 Liu Xiong defeated river Jihu chiefs who crossed to fight.

sentences.zh: 建德五年，高祖敗齊師于晉州，乘勝逐北，齊人所棄甲仗，未暇收斂，稽胡乘閑竊出，竝盜而有之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jiande Emperor Gaozu defeated Qi troops at Jin Prefecture, pursued north taking advantage of victory; armor and weapons the Qi men abandoned were not yet gathered when the Jihu seized the interval to slip out and all stole and possessed them.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiande year 5 after defeating Qi at Jinzhou, Jihu looted abandoned Qi arms.

sentences.zh: 乃立蠡升孫沒鐸為主，號聖武皇帝，年曰石平。

translations.literal: They then set Li Sheng's grandson Moduo as lord, styled Holy Martial Emperor, era name Shiping.
translations.idiomatic: They made Moduo, grandson of Li Sheng, Holy Martial Emperor with era Shiping.

sentences.zh: 六年，高祖定東夏，將討之，議欲窮其巢穴。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Emperor Gaozu pacified eastern Xia and was about to campaign against them; deliberation wished to exhaust their nests.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 Emperor Wu planned to root them out entirely.

sentences.zh: 齊王憲以為種類旣多，又山谷阻絕，王師一舉，未可盡除。

translations.literal: Prince of Qi Xian thought their kinds were already numerous and mountain valleys blocked and cut off; one stroke of the royal army could not remove them all.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xian argued their numbers and mountains made total extermination impossible.

sentences.zh: 且當剪其魁首，余加慰撫。

translations.literal: One should rather cut off their chiefs and soothe the rest.
translations.idiomatic: He urged killing the leaders and pacifying the rest.

sentences.zh: 高祖然之，乃以憲為行軍元帥，督行軍總管趙王招、譙王儉、滕王逌等討之。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu approved and therefore made Xian Mobile Corps Marshal, supervising Mobile Corps Commanders Prince of Zhao Zhao, Prince of Qiao Jian, Prince of Teng You, and others to campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and made Prince Xian marshal with princes Zhao, Qiao, and Teng under him.

sentences.zh: 憲軍次馬邑，乃分道俱進。

translations.literal: Xian's army halted at Mayi and then divided routes to advance together.
translations.idiomatic: Xian halted at Mayi and advanced on several routes.

sentences.zh: 沒鐸遣其黨天柱守河東，又遣其大帥穆支據河西，規欲分守險要，掎角憲軍。

translations.literal: Moduo sent his faction Tianzhu to hold Hedong and sent his great chief Muzhi to hold Hexi, planning to divide and hold strategic points and pinch Xian's army.
translations.idiomatic: Moduo held Hedong and Hexi to pinch Xian's army.

sentences.zh: 憲命譙王儉攻天柱，滕王逌擊穆支，竝破之，斬首萬餘級。

translations.literal: Xian ordered Prince of Qiao Jian to attack Tianzhu and Prince of Teng You to strike Muzhi; both were defeated and more than ten thousand heads cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Princes Jian and You broke both wings with ten thousand killed.

sentences.zh: 趙王招又擒沒鐸，餘衆盡降。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhao Zhao again captured Moduo and the remainder all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhao captured Moduo and the rest surrendered.

sentences.zh: 宣政元年，汾州稽胡帥劉受羅千復反，越王盛督諸軍討擒之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuanzheng the Fenzhou Jihu chief Liu Shouluoqian rebelled again; Prince of Yue Sheng supervised the armies, campaigned, and seized him.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of  Liu Shouluoqian rebelled; Prince Sheng captured him.

sentences.zh: 自是寇盜頗息。

translations.literal: From this bandits and robbers were largely stilled.
translations.idiomatic: After that raiding largely ceased.

sentences.zh: 庫莫奚

translations.literal: Kumo Xi
translations.idiomatic: Kumo Xi

sentences.zh: 庫莫奚，鮮卑之別種也。

translations.literal: Kumo Xi were a separate branch of the Xianbei.
translations.idiomatic: The Kumo Xi were a Xianbei offshoot.

sentences.zh: 其先為慕容晃所破，竄於松漠之間。

translations.literal: Their forebears were broken by Murong Huang and fled among the pine deserts.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Huang defeated them and they fled to the pine deserts.

sentences.zh: 後種類漸多，分為五部：一曰辱紇主，二曰莫賀弗，三曰契個，四曰木昆，五曰室得。

translations.literal: Later their kind gradually multiplied and divided into five divisions: first Ruohezhu, second Mohefu, third Qige, fourth Mukun, fifth Shide.
translations.idiomatic: They later split into five divisions: Ruohezhu, Mohefu, Qige, Mukun, and Shide.

sentences.zh: 每部置俟

translations.literal: Each division set a qi
translations.idiomatic: Each division appointed a qi

translations.literal: (Chi)
translations.idiomatic: Chi, an erroneous character; see the emended jin below.

sentences.zh: 〔斤〕一人。

translations.literal: [Jin] one man.
translations.idiomatic: Each division appointed one jin officer.

sentences.zh: 有阿會氏者，最為豪帥，五部皆受其節度。

translations.literal: There was the Ahui clan, the most powerful chieftain, and all five divisions received their regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The Ahui clan ruled all five divisions.

sentences.zh: 役屬於突厥，而數與契丹相攻。

translations.literal: They served the Turks yet repeatedly attacked the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: They served the Turks and fought the Khitan repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 虜獲財畜，因而行賞。

translations.literal: Captives and livestock seized were then used for rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Loot was shared as reward.

sentences.zh: 死者則以葦薄裹尸，懸之樹上。

translations.literal: The dead were wrapped in reed mats and hung on trees.
translations.idiomatic: The dead were wrapped in reeds and hung in trees.

sentences.zh: 大統五年，遣使獻其方物。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Datong they sent envoys presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong year 5 they sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：凡民肖形天地，稟靈陰陽，愚智本於自然，剛柔繫於水土。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: All people take form from Heaven and Earth and receive spirit from yin and yang; foolishness and wisdom root in nature, hardness and softness tie to water and soil.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: All people take form from Heaven and Earth and yin and yang; wit and folly, hardness and softness, follow land and water.

sentences.zh: 故雨露所會，風流所通，九川為紀，五嶽作鎮，此之謂諸夏。

translations.literal: Thus where rain and dew meet and winds and currents pass, the nine rivers form their rule and the five peaks stand as pillars—this is called the many Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Where rain and dew fall and winds blow, bounded by nine rivers and five peaks, lies civilization—the many Xia.

sentences.zh: 生其地者，則仁義出焉。

translations.literal: Those born in that land then produce benevolence and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Those born there produce benevolence and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 昧穀、嵎夷、孤竹、北戶，限以丹徼紫塞，隔以滄海交河，此之謂荒裔。

translations.literal: Meigu, Yuyi, Guzhu, and Beihu, bounded by cinnabar frontier and purple passes, separated by the blue sea and the Jiao River—this is called the wild periphery.
translations.idiomatic: Meigu, Yuyi, Guzhu, and Beihu, beyond the red frontier and purple passes, beyond sea and Jiao River, are the wild periphery.

sentences.zh: 感其氣者，則凶德成焉。

translations.literal: Those moved by its qi then form fierce virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Those shaped by its air turn fierce.

sentences.zh: 若夫九夷八狄，種落繁熾；

translations.literal: As for the nine Yi and eight Di, tribes flourish;
translations.idiomatic: The nine Yi and eight Di multiply;

sentences.zh: 七戎六蠻，充牣邊鄙。

translations.literal: the seven Rong and six Man fill the border marches.
translations.idiomatic: seven Rong and six Man pack the frontier.

sentences.zh: 雖風土殊俗，嗜欲不同，至於貪而無厭，狠而好亂，彊則旅拒，弱則稽服，其揆一也。

translations.literal: Although wind and soil differ and appetites differ, as to being greedy without satiety, fierce and fond of disorder, when strong they gather to resist, when weak they bow in submission—the measure is one.
translations.idiomatic: Customs differ, yet all are greedy, fierce, rebellious when strong and submissive when weak—the pattern is one.

sentences.zh: 斯蓋天之所命，使其然乎。

translations.literal: This is probably Heaven's command, making them so.
translations.idiomatic: Perhaps Heaven made them so.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七一年十一月版《周書》為本校。

translations.literal: The full text uses the Zhonghua Shuju November 1971 edition of the Book of Zhou as the base for collation.
translations.idiomatic: This edition collates against the Zhonghua Shuju Book of Zhou (November 1971).
